new_roles.title: VP, Foundry Operations
new_roles.description:
If you are looking for a challenging and exciting career in the world of technology, then look no further. Skyworks is an innovator of high-performance analog semiconductors whose solutions are powering the wireless networking revolution. Through our broad technology expertise and one of the most extensive product portfolios in the industry, we are Connecting Everyone and Everything, All the Time.
 
 
At Skyworks, you will find a fast-paced environment with a strong focus on global collaboration, minimal layers of management, and the freedom to make meaningful contributions in a setting that encourages creative thinking. We are excited about the opportunity to work with you and glad you want to be part of a team of talented individuals who together are changing the way the world communicates.
 
 
Requisition ID: 79081
 
 
**Description**
The Vice President of Foundry Operations provides global leadership for Skyworks' external wafer-foundry manufacturing network. The executive owns the operating system that converts technology and product roadmaps into predictable supply, benchmark yield and zero-defect quality, competitive cost, timely NPI ramps, and resilient high-volume production.
 
 
The role integrates Foundry Operations with Foundry Engineering and Supplier Quality, serving as the primary executive interface to strategic foundry partners and aligning Business Units, Design, Product Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Finance, and Foundry Technology.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
Global Foundry Strategy & Executive Supplier Leadership
 
 
Define and execute the external foundry operating strategy aligned with product, technology, supply, cost, continuity, compliance, and resilienc
 
 
Lead executive supplier relationships, governance, business reviews, escalations, and joint improvement roadmaps with strategic foundry partners
 
 
Represent Global Operations with foundry executive leadership, communicating performance expectations, transformation priorities, audits, Si technology node HVM readiness, and joint improvement commitments
 
 
Delivery Execution
 
 
Own operational execution from purchase-order issuance through wafer delivery and goods receipt, with transparent supply visibility and disciplined recovery plans
 
 
Manage cycle-time performance, technology transfer and capacity expansion readiness, production ramps, and hot lot management. Partner with SCM, Sourcing, Engineering, and Business Units to protect Skyworks revenue
 
 
Ensure supply plans are feasible and on schedule, with transparent visibility, rapid escalation, and disciplined recovery plans that reflect revenue, absorption, manufacturing cost, and ROI
 
 
Foundry Engineering, Yield, Quality & Process Control
 
 
Drive benchmark probe and final-test yield across external foundries through defect-density benchmarks, product data, and structured yield roadmaps, backed by robust in-line metrology, PCM, SPC/WECO, FDC, and critical-parameter controls
 
 
Establish a zero-defect, source-containment culture and systematically improve Mean-Time-to-Detect and Mean-Time-to-React using real-time indicators of emerging risk
 
 
Quality-excursion containment, root-cause analysis, material disposition, corrective action, verification of non-recurrence (8D reviews), and foundry change-control governance
 
 
NTI to NPI and HVM Ramp Readiness
 
 
Global Operations quality rigor and design for manufacturing through an end-to-end Foundry Ramp Readiness system (NTI oversight, pre-ramp readiness, ramp verification, clean launch, HVM stabilization, and critical production mass) with defined gates, ownership, and escalation
 
 
Verify foundry capability, capacity, yield, quality, cycle time, and supply before ramp and customer commitments, partnering with Foundry Technology, Design, Product Engineering, Quality, SCM, and Business Units to close gaps and protect schedules
 
 
**Responsibilities Continued**
Competitive Performance & Operations Excellence
 
 
Deploy and sustain the Performance Management System (PMS) within Foundry Operations
 
 
Establish competitive benchmarks, aggressive KPI targets, review cadence, and continuous-improvement roadmaps across technology, cost, productivity, quality, yield, cycle time, delivery, and responsiveness
 
 
Cost, Productivity & Financial Performance
 
 
Own foundry VAVE (Value Analysis and Value Engineering) cost and productivity roadmaps, yield improvement, cycle time, capacity utilization, and supplier value creation
 
 
Partner with Sourcing and Supply chain on capacity commitments, long-term agreements, and NRE, balancing cost, quality, delivery, technology access, continuity, and compliance in supplier decisions
 
 
Digital Operations, Analytics & Organizational Leadership
 
 
Automate repetitive workflows and provide early warnings of excursions, delivery misses, capacity constraints, and cycle-time changes
 
 
Use analytics and a single source of operational truth to prioritize action, monitor PDCA closure, and improve decision speed and accountability
 
 
Lead and develop a global, matrixed, and multicultural team spanning fab operations, engineering, yield, supplier quality, and analytics; build succession depth and critical capabilities
 
 
Communicate decisions, trade-offs, risks, and recovery plans with executive presence across internal leaders, foundries, foundry suppliers, and, when required, Skyworks customers
 
 
**Required Experience And Skills**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, or a related discipline required; master's degree, MBA, or advanced technical degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive semiconductor manufacturing, foundry, technology development, product engineering, supply chain, or operations leadership experience, including significant global responsibility.
* Deep end-to-end understanding of wafer fabrication, critical process modules, design/process interaction, yield ramp, process control, quality systems, NPI, and high-volume manufacturing.
* Demonstrated success managing external foundries, executive supplier relationships, capacity, technology transfers, production ramps, quality excursions, and cross-functional recovery programs.
* Proven ability to use operational data, analytics, and insights to drive execution; experience with Power BI or comparable business-intelligence tools is valued.
* Executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to operate at strategic and hands-on levels across technical, commercial, and operational issues.
* Willingness to travel domestically and internationally.

**Desired Experience And Skills**

* Strategic thinking and semiconductor business acumen
* People and organizational leadership
* Change leadership and operational transformation
* Decisive, data-based judgment under uncertainty
* Customer focus and cross-functional influence
* Accountability for results, ethics, safety, and quality

The typical base pay range for this role across the U.S. is currently USD $206,900 - $454,100 per year. Starting base pay will depend on relevant experience and skills, training and education, business needs, market demands, the ultimate job duties and requirements, and work location. Skyworks has different base pay ranges for different work locations in the U.S. Benefits include access to healthcare benefits (including a premium-free medical plan option), a 401(k) plan and company match, an employee stock purchase plan, paid time off (including vacation, sick/wellness, parental leave), among others. Employees are eligible to participate in an incentive plan, and certain roles are also eligible for additional awards, including recognition and stock. These incentives and awards are based on individual and/or company performance.
 
 
Skyworks is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Skyworks strives to create an accessible workplace; if you need an accommodation due to a disability, please contact us at accommodations@skyworksinc.com.

new_roles.title: Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**Bold Thinking. World Changing.**
At SkyWater, our ingenuity helps improve lives around the world by manufacturing U.S. made semiconductors that are essential ingredients of modern life. Automotive safety enhancements, life-saving medical devices, consumer electronics and American security require semiconductors. Working in our Minnesota headquarters, Florida, or Texas location — employees join together to improve the world.
 
 
**Explore what’s possible.**
Joining our U.S. - based team means contributing to and learning about the commercialization of some of the most exciting technologies the world has ever seen. We are turning “science fiction” into everyday reality through technologies such as superconducting, 3D integrated circuits or computer chips, carbon nanotubes, photonic logic devices, micro electro-mechanical systems and other emerging device topologies. We manufacture products for aerospace and defense, medical, automotive, consumer and industrial markets, to name a few. Our customers include emerging leaders who rely on our intellectual property security and quality manufacturing services.
 
 
**Step into the future.**
SkyWater’s values of Integrity, Excellence, Collaboration, Empowerment and Growth Mindset guide us to cultivate an empowered, learning environment. We also invest in developing highly skilled, dedicated employees — and employees who are entering the workforce for the first time, from the military, and a variety of educational backgrounds.
 
 
**Are you bold thinking?**
Find your place on our team and help us change the world!
 
 
**Primary Objective**
Join an innovative semiconductor manufacturing organization at the forefront of advanced technology and manufacturing excellence. The Director of Integrated Fab Manufacturing owns the operational, financial, and strategic leadership of the Bloomington fabrication facility, including the Advanced Technology Services (ATS) Process Engineering Technician team. This role ensures the factory achieves world-class safety, quality, output, cycle time, and cost performance while directing a 24/7 organization and partnering across engineering, planning, and quality teams to meet all customer and business commitments.
 
 
In this role, you will be responsible for the end-to-end operational execution, strategic planning, budgetary ownership, and leadership to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient semiconductor manufacturing. You will be responsible for driving absolute excellence across safety, quality, output, cost optimization, and ensuring smooth production flow to consistently meet internal and external customer quality and on-time delivery (OTD) commitments, and fab velocity metrics / key performance indicators (KPIs).
 
 
The successful candidate will own the organizational design and talent strategy for their organization, serving as a role model and lead a highly matrixed organization consisting of the Manufacturing team, Process Engineering Technicians group, and Flow Engineers. This role is expected to partner closely with Program Managers, Technical Leads, Wafer Planning, Manufacturing, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development teams to improve operational performance, resolve manufacturing constraints, and deliver business objectives. This leader will play a critical role in transforming factory capabilities to meet strict customer commitments and flexible demand by influencing long-range capacity and setting standards for the MN fab operations organization.
 
 
**Major Areas Of Accountability**

* Operations Leadership: Lead the daily and long-term operational execution in the fab, as well as the ATS technician and flow engineer teams to meet all production starts, output targets, yield expectations, cycle time goals, and quality standards, including setting clear priorities for the organization. Direct, develop, and coach the 24/7 operations teams—including Production, ATS Process Engineering Technicians, and Flow Engineers—to ensure capability, accountability, and organizational readiness.
* Team Leadership: Lead, develop, and empower the Production team, Process Engineering Technicians and Flow Engineers to provide effective manufacturing support, maintain production continuity, and resolve process and workflow issues
* Budgetary Responsibility: Own the fab operating budget, including labor, materials, maintenance, and operational spending; drive cost-reduction initiatives and evaluate capital investments using ROI-based decision-making.
* Wafer Planning and Customer Delivery: Partner with Wafer Planning and Program Management to align schedules, capacity, and customer priorities; identify delivery risks and oversee recovery plans to maintain on time delivery (OTD) performance.
* Manufacturing Performance: Partner with Industrial Engineers, and drive continuous improvement in throughput, cycle time, WIP management, yield, quality, equipment availability, and manufacturing cost using data-driven decision-making and structured problem-solving.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Coordinate with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Equipment Engineering, Quality, and Technology Development to resolve production constraints, improve equipment readiness, and maintain stable manufacturing operations.
* Operational Excellence: Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), including customer OTD, cycle time, throughput, equipment availability, and quality. Promote standardization, disciplined execution, effective escalation, and continuous improvement.
* Talent Development: Build a high-performing organization through coaching, accountability, collaboration, and development of technical and operational talent. Responsible for the organizational design and talent strategy of these teams, with a focus on cultivating and retaining key talent, developing future leaders and preparing current leaders for the next level role.

**Required Qualifications**- Education: Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Physics, or related technical discipline.
- Experience: Minimum 12 years in semiconductor manufacturing or operations; minimum 5+ years leading fab operations in a senior manager or director capacity within a 24/7 manufacturing environment.
- Skills:

* Demonstrated ability to improve manufacturing performance (throughput, cycle time, yield, cost, and customer delivery).
* Expertise in wafer planning, WIP management, or production scheduling.
* Strong capability in statistical process control (SPC), structured problem-solving, and data-driven decision-making.
* Demonstrated leadership with large technical teams, with an ability to communicate and collaborate cross-functionally, delivering results in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

* Ability to enter the cleanroom in full PPE to provide technical and operational support.
* Ability to navigate multi-level fab environments, including prolonged walking and standing when needed.

*The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job.*

* Education: Master’s or PhD in a relevant technical discipline.
* Experience: Deep knowledge of advanced Complimentary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) nodes, fab toolsets (Lithography, Etch, Diffusion, Thin Films, Chemical Mechanical Polish, Metrology, Metals), and factory automation systems.
* Skills: Experience driving major manufacturing transformations, automation or digitization initiatives, or large-scale capacity improvements.

new_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing
new_roles.description:
**About Us:**
Alliance Machine Systems International, LLC is a privately held company with over 35 years of history dedicated to providing corrugated box manufacturing machines and services to the changing industry. As the paperboard packaging industry's premier global supplier of productivity-enhancing process machinery and systems, we supply innovative designs, intelligent automation, and optimized workflow, coupled with highly responsive parts and service support. Our United States and Europe based engineering, manufacturing, sales and service operations provide a global support system covering the full product portfolio of Alliance, Serco, TEI, ASC, Pallmac, J&L and Tanabe machines.
 
 
Barry-Wehmiller is a diversified global supplier of engineering consulting and manufacturing technology for the packaging, corrugating, sheeting and paper-converting industries. By blending people-centric leadership with disciplined operational strategies and purpose-driven growth, Barry-Wehmiller has become a $3 billion organization with nearly 12,000 team members united by a common belief: to use the power of business to build a better world.
 
 
**Job Description:**
***THIS IS AN ONSITE ROLE LOCATED IN SPOKANE, WASHINGTON.***
**Job Overview:**
Alliance Machine Systems Int is seeking a Director of Manufacturing to lead manufacturing performance and operational scale across its North American production sites.
 
 
This is a considerable leadership role for an experienced manufacturing leader who understands the complexity of producing industrial automation equipment and engineered systems.
 
 
The Director of Manufacturing will be responsible for improving the connection between engineering, production, quality, supply chain, and customer delivery.
 
 
The successful candidate will lead a manufacturing environment where products may include complex electrical, mechanical, robotic and controls. The role will involve managing high-mix production, engineered-to-order or configure-to-order manufacturing, and the delivery of technically sophisticated equipment to major industrial customers.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities:**

* Lead manufacturing operations across the company’s production facilities.
* Set standards for safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, and cost.
* Improve the transfer of products and projects from engineering into manufacturing.
* Increase capacity while maintaining quality, delivery, and customer performance.
* Improve on-time delivery, lead times, throughput, and gross margin.
* Strengthen production planning, scheduling, capacity planning, and work-in-progress control.
* Manage critical components, suppliers, and long-lead materials with procurement and supply chain teams.
* Establish scalable processes for complex, high-mix, engineered-to-order automation products and systems.
* Support new product introduction and design-for-manufacture initiatives.
* Improve collaboration across sales, engineering, project management, procurement, and manufacturing.
* Lead recovery plans for delayed or strategically important projects.
* Establish clear manufacturing and performance-management KPIs.
* Develop plant managers, production managers, and operational teams.
* Support facility expansion, automation investment, capital planning, and potential upcoming new-site development.
* Partner with the executive team on manufacturing strategy, capacity, organizational design, and long-term growth.

**Requirements:**

* 12+ years’ experience in manufacturing, operations, or plant leadership within an industrial manufacturing environment.
* At least 7 years in manufacturing leadership, with direct responsibility for manufacturing performance.
* Experience within industrial automation, robotics, machinery, electrical equipment, motion control, or engineered capital equipment manufacturing.
* Direct leadership of manufacturing operations, rather than engineering or project delivery alone.
* Experience with complex, high-mix, engineered-to-order, configure-to-order, or project-based production.
* A proven record of improving delivery, quality, productivity, capacity, cost, and gross margin.
* Experience leading cross-functional teams across production, quality, planning, and supply chain.
* Strong understanding of the transition from engineering and product design into manufacturing.
* Experience leading managers and developing scalable operational structures.
* Working knowledge of ERP, MRP, production planning, scheduling, and manufacturing-performance systems.
* Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills across engineering, sales, project management, supply chain, service, and executive leadership.
* Willingness to travel to US manufacturing sites, suppliers, and customers as required.

Compensation: $150,000-180,000 base salary
 
 
Benefits: Alliance offers a competitive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life insurance, disability insurance, 401K with employer match, PTO, paid holidays and a bonus program.
 
 
*At Barry-Wehmiller we recognize that people come with a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the technical requirements of a job. If your experience is close to what you see listed here, please still consider applying. We know that our differences often can bring about innovation, excellence and meaningful work—therefore, people from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply to our positions. Please let us know if you require reasonable accommodations during the interview process.*
Barry-Wehmiller is an equal opportunity employer. M/F/D/V This organization uses E-Verify.
 
 
Applicants may be subject to pre-employment screening which may include drug screening, reference checks, employment verifications, background screening and/or skills assessments.
 
 
**Company:**
Alliance

**Job Description**
**Director Operations for Drug Product**
Do you aspire to secure a critical role in the production of biologics-based medicines? Are you excited to lead dynamic teams in a state-of-the-art facility that brings transformative biotech treatments to patients globally? We invite you to become a part of our journey as the Director Operations for Drug Product. This role offers you the chance to contribute to the site's development and wield technical leadership to ensure successful GMP manufacturing.
 
 
**Principle Roles & Responsibilities / Accountabilities**

* The Director, Operations – Drug Product plays a critical part in strategic project realization of the Wilmington Biotech facility, a new hi-potent facility in our company's Biologic manufacturing network, ensuring that site’s mission and objectives are effectively achieved, consistent with our company's requirements to ensure compliance, safety and reliable supply to our customers.
* As a key member of the Site Leadership Team, you'll have the opportunity to shape site and organizational strategies, overseeing drug product manufacturing for commercial and new product introductions.
* Be part of facility start-up to manufacture high-potent products, eg antibody drug conjugates (ADCs)
* You will work collaboratively with cross-functional teams to streamline technology transfers and commercial approvals, meanwhile nurturing and empowering your operations team.
* You'll get to foster a culture of continuous learning and improvement, leading or supporting various site functional and cross-functional structures for departmental alignment.
* Tackling resource constraints and needs, you will champion operational and technical excellence for efficient production and implement Lean principles for process optimization.
* Upholding our Manufacturing Division Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, you will manage relevant quality topics, and ensure permanent inspection readiness.
* You will oversee financial forecasts and workload for departmental cost improvements, aligning with capital and expense targets while contributing to sustainability and cost reduction initiatives.
* You will have the chance to leverage digital tools for operational efficiency and informed decision-making, keeping pace with emerging digital technologies relevant to manufacturing processes.
* You will be accountable for achieving onsite Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), monitoring and striving to improve performance metrics related to hiring, uptime, training, change controls, investigations, CAPAs, yield, volume, production cadence, operational availability, and more.

**Qualification And Experience**
**Required Experience and Skills:**

* A degree or equivalent in Engineering, Science, Technical, or other relevant fields: Bachelor’s degree + 12 years industry experience Or Masters + 10 years Or PhD + 8 years
* 6 or more years demonstrated leadership ability and experience managing, coaching, and mentoring high-performing cross function teams.
* Demonstrated experience in a biotech/vaccines/pharma manufacturing site, project, or other relevant roles, specifically drug product sterile manufacturing.
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing clinical and commercial products.
* Understanding of cGMP requirements for commercial high-potent ADC manufacturing of drug product

**Preferred Experience And Skills**

* Sterile manufacturing leadership & operations, with preferred multi-product experience.
* A leader who inspires, coaches, and fosters a high-performance organizational culture.
* A continuous learner who cultivates a culture of ongoing development within your team.
* An innovative thinker with excellent decision-making and problem-solving skills.
* Experienced in leading highly effective cross-functional teams with a passion for shaping the future of our organization.
* Capable of influencing and building relationships across organizational layers, as well as externally with partners.

new_roles.title: Plant Director
new_roles.description:
**At The Cheesecake Factory Bakery, We Don't Do Ordinary!**
Nothing is scaled down. Not the pride, not the fun, and definitely not the teamwork. Here, you'll lead great people, drive meaningful impact, and help shape the future of our business while supporting the bakery and restaurant teams behind the iconic cheesecakes our guests enjoy every day. That's the kind of culture that has earned us a place on Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For® list every year since 2014.

**The Plant Director**
provides strategic and operational leadership for a three-shift, seven-day manufacturing facility encompassing approximately 160 full-time, non-union employees. Leading all aspects of production and packaging operations, you will drive performance, efficiency, quality, and continuous improvement across scheduling, logistics, pre-scaling, mixing, depositing, baking, decorating, and packaging to support the Bakery's operational and business objectives.

They utilize excellent leadership, analytical, management, and technical skills, abilities, and behaviors to drive performance in key areas such as people, safety, quality, service, and cost, aligned with measurable objectives and the Company’s Mission, Vision, and Values. The Director also assists with business continuity in the absence of the VP of Operations.

**You’ll thrive in this position if you are:**

* **Service oriented:**
 you are a people person who is systematic and trustworthy and interacts constructively with peers or teams of various levels demonstrating strong, positive communication skills.
* **Driven by results:**
 you are conscientious and persistent about delivering timely, high-quality deliverables, and performing all job functions safely while following instructions.
* **Improvement focused:**
 you never turn off the thought “how can I do this better/faster”.
* **Pressure resistant:**
 you have ice in your veins while under pressure. Maintaining a positive outlook at work while the heat is on is never an issue for you.

**Here’s more of what you’ll get to do:**

* Maintain positive employee relations through respectful, open, and effective two-way communication at the individual and team levels.
* Partner with human resources and training departments to develop, implement, and maintain effective training and development programs that support performance goals and provide a satisfying work environment.
* Maintain a fair and professional work environment that balances business objectives with quality-of-work-life factors for employees.
* Work with Human Resources to ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and company policies, while driving improvements in employee performance as measured by turnover rate, attendance, and feedback mechanisms.
* Oversee production planning and scheduling to optimize service and efficiency, balancing resources such as crewing, materials, and equipment with other department managers.
* Supervise the development of synchronized crewing, equipment setup, and materials preparation plans to ensure schedule attainment and optimize capacity utilization.
* Manage timekeeping, labor efficiency, and plant productivity in compliance with legal and company policies, aiming to minimize overtime and control non-productive line time.
* Collaborate with the Plant Engineer to ensure preventive and emergency maintenance efforts are effective, minimizing downtime and optimizing machine performance.
* Manage material usage to ensure minimal waste and maximum yield, while maintaining strict adherence to product quality standards and inventory management.
* Monitor spending and manage operations within approved budget levels, while driving improvements in cost performance through labor productivity, waste reduction, and yield maximization.
* Ensure disciplined compliance with product and process quality standards, food safety, and regulatory requirements, striving for “EXCELLENT” or “SUPERIOR” scores in third-party audits.
* Lead plant safety efforts, including co-chairing the Safety Steering Committee, safety inspections, and training, while driving improvements in safety performance as measured by injury frequency and workers' compensation data.
* Participate in business plan development, budgeting processes, and plant-level meetings to ensure effective communication and alignment with operational goals.
* Ability to transform the facility into a CI culture driven by people, process and equipment/technology.
* Ensure the utilization of 4-step process to drive result in sustainability which are Huddles, Daily meeting, utilization of Red Zone and Sic meetings.

**What we require:**

* Minimum of 15 years of experience in food manufacturing management, preferably in the bakery/dessert industry, with demonstrated success at the Plant Manager or Director of Manufacturing/Operations level.
* Bachelor’s degree (MBA a Plus)
* Strong experience with food safety, food process equipment, and regulations.
* Strong experience with emergency preparedness and emergency response plans and procedures.
* Familiar with regulatory and safety codes, including USDA, FDA, and OSHA regulations.
* Knowledge and demonstrated skill in lean manufacturing, Kaizen, kitting, and Six Sigma techniques.
* Prior experience with direct responsibility for a large-scale P&L.
* Strong and effective strategic management skills, including long-range planning, organizing, communicating, influencing, gathering and using information, and motivating a team to achieve results. Ability to use, and teach others to use, various analytical tools and techniques.
* Demonstrated mentoring skills.

**What we offer:**

* Eligible for annual bonus
* Eligible for annual equity grants
* Medical, Dental & Vision
* Eligible for benefits first day of the month following date of hire
* 401K with company match
* 3 weeks of vacation which increases to 4 weeks starting in your 5th year
* 5 days of sick time per year (first year prorated)
* Tuition Reimbursement of $2,500 for qualified programs
* Adoption Assistance Benefit of $2,500
* 25%-35% discount when dining as a guest
* Reusable gift card loaded annually for your dining enjoyment

**About the Company:**

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery creates over 35,000 delicious cheesecakes per day across our two facilities in Calabasas, CA and Rocky Mount, NC plus other baked products for our restaurants, international licensees, and third-party bakery customers.

The Cheesecake Factory Bakery is a subsidiary of The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated. Recognized as a Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® since 2014, The Cheesecake Factory Incorporated is a global $3.8 billion public company with more than 370 casual dining restaurants and over 48,000 staff members.

We are an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive and welcoming workplace for all. We welcome applicants from a wide variety of identities, ideas, perspectives, backgrounds and experiences to apply. The Cheesecake Factory offers reasonable accommodation to job applicants with disabilities.

#SoCheesecake #LifeAtCheesecake

To notify of a non-compliant job posting, please send a notice to ats@thecheesecakefactory.com.

new_roles.title: Director - New Site Manufacturing-Electric Propulsion
new_roles.description:
**Application Close Date**
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.
 
 
At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.
 
 
We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. This position will directly impact the history of space exploration and require your commitment and detailed attention toward safe and repeatable space flight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.
 
 
We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!
 
 
Blue Origin is scaling production of its electric propulsion systems. We are hiring a Director to own the manufacturing outcome for that product line and to carry it from development hardware into rate production.
 
 
You will be the single-threaded leader for Operations of this program: one person accountable for rate, quality, cost, and people, with full authority over the entire in-program production flow.
 
 
This is a build-it role, not a run-it role. You will define the value streams, stand up integration with support organizations, and build the team that runs the line — working concurrently with an active design program rather than behind a frozen one.
 
 
**Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To**

* Own the strategy, roadmap, and priorities for successful manufacturing outcomes of the electric propulsion thruster line — delivery rate, quality, cost, and the people who produce it.
* Build the production organization. Define the value streams, stand up production control and manufacturing engineering, and hire and develop the leadership beneath you as the program scales.
* Own the get-to-rate plan. Define the path from development build to sustained rate production, and demonstrate cycle time at the rate-readiness gate as a committed acceptance number rather than a projection.
* Lead the transition from development build into rate production, including the qualification of tooling, processes, and work instructions required to produce repeatably at rate.
* Drive producibility into the product during design, rather than absorbing it on the floor later. Own the manufacturing view of the bill of materials as the product configuration evolves.
* Establish and own the program's working interfaces with quality, supply chain, material planning, and test operations.
* Build and manage the program's manufacturing operating budget and capital plan, owning responsibility for product delivery at cost and rate.
* Set the safety and quality culture for a new production team, and hold it as the organization grows.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in an engineering or technical discipline.
* 12+ years of experience in manufacturing, production, supply chain, or operations, including 5+ years leading manufacturing organizations.
* Direct, hands-on experience taking a new product or production line from development into rate production.
* Experience carrying a product through a production-readiness or rate-readiness gate, and owning the cycle-time and capability evidence presented at it.
* Experience building an organization — defining structure, hiring leaders, and developing a team through significant growth.
* Line management of both salaried professionals and craft or technician populations.
* Demonstrated ability to operate in ambiguity: making defensible assumptions and moving forward on an incomplete definition, then correcting as information arrives.
* Ability to travel frequently, up to approximately 35%, to other Blue Origin sites.
* Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* 15+ years of manufacturing and operations experience.
* Propulsion, spacecraft, satellite, or other high-reliability low-volume hardware experience.
* Experience transitioning a product from low-volume, high-mix build into repeatable rate production.
* Demonstrated cycle-time or throughput improvement with measured results.
* Experience standing up production at a new or greenfield manufacturing site.
* Experience managing a build against a bill of materials that changed materially during production ramp.
* Formal lean or continuous-improvement training, with applied results on a production line.
* Master’s degree in engineering or technical field, or MBA.

**Base Pay Range For**
WA applicants is $203,165.00 - $284,430.30
 
 
**Other Site Ranges May Differ**
**Culture Statement**
Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
 
 
**Export Control Regulations**
Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
 
 
**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
* Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
* Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
* Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**
Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. new_roles.title: Sr. Manager Manufacturing Engineer
new_roles.description:
**Work Schedule**
Standard (Mon-Fri)
 
 
**Environmental Conditions**
Adherence to all Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) Safety Standards
 
 
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
 
 
DESCRIPTION:
 
 
As a Sr. Manager, Manufacturing Engineering at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you will guide and support engineering teams to drive operational excellence and innovation across our manufacturing facilities. You will provide strategic direction and technical leadership for manufacturing processes, automation initiatives, and continuous improvement projects while ensuring compliance with quality and regulatory requirements. Working collaboratively with cross-functional teams, you'll optimize production efficiency, implement new technologies, and deliver solutions that enable our mission of making the world healthier, cleaner and safer.
 
 
REQUIREMENTS:
 
 

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in regulated manufacturing environments (pharmaceutical, medical device, or related industries)
* Preferred Fields of Study: Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Chemical) or related technical field. Strong focus on Automation required.
* Industry certifications in Six Sigma, PMP, or related areas are beneficial
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing technical teams and facilitating organizational change
* Demonstrated success implementing automation, digitalization and continuous improvement initiatives
* Strong understanding of cGMP, ISO standards and regulatory compliance requirements
* Experience with new product introductions, technology transfers and process validation
* Expertise in lean manufacturing principles, Six Sigma methodology and practical process improvements (PPI)
* Demonstrated ability to develop and execute strategic plans aligned with business objectives
* Strong project management skills and experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives
* Excellent analytical and problem-solving capabilities with data-driven decision making
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills to engage stakeholders at all levels
* Proficiency with manufacturing systems, automation platforms and quality tools
* Ability to manage multiple priorities effectively
* Experience with capital project planning, budgeting and resource allocation
* Relocation: Relocation assistance is not available for this position.
* Work Authorization: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States without current or future employer-sponsored work authorization.
* Pre-Employment Screening: Employment is contingent upon successful completion of all applicable pre-employment requirements, including a background check and drug screening, in accordance with company policy and applicable law.

**Compensation And Benefits**
The salary range estimated for this position based in New Jersey is $155,100.00–$232,650.00.
 
 
This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:
 
 

* A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
* Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
* At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy
* Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan
* Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount

For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Plant Operations
new_roles.description:
At WK Kellogg Co, we exist to create joy and connection to inspire Gr-r-reat days. We believe that doing good is always good for business and we have stood for this since Kellogg Company was founded more than 120 years ago. We are passionate about doing our part to make nutritious foods, create social connectivity and respect natural resources. Together, these actions create positive progress for people and the planet – today and for years to come. We have big plans for how we are going to accomplish this, and we would love for you to join us in this effort.
 
 
**The most compelling leadership opportunities aren’t always about stepping into something already built. Sometimes they’re about helping shape what comes next.**
The
**Senior Manager, Plant Operations**
leads the strategic and operational direction of multiple business units within a high-performing, large-scale, 24/7 manufacturing operation, and line-centric manufacturing platform.
 
 
This role drives excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people development by empowering Operations Managers, Supervisors, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.
 
 
**You won’t simply inherit an operation. You’ll have the opportunity to help build what comes next.**
**Working Relationships Include**

* Reports to: Plant Director
* Supervises: Operations Managers and Supervisors
* Peer Relationships: KSUM, Quality Manager, Sr. RM Manager, HR Manager, EHS Manager, E& F Manager, KIWS Coach
* Key Contacts: Internal – Plant Leadership Team, Corporate Operations, Engineering, KIWS, HR; External – Vendors, Contractors, and Corporate Support Functions

**Here’s What You Will Be Doing**

* Strategic Leadership: Set direction and priorities for assigned business units, ensuring alignment with plant goals and corporate strategy.
* Team Development: Lead, coach, and develop Operations Managers and Supervisor to build high-performing teams and future leaders.
* Operational Oversight: Ensure consistent execution of production plans and consistently deliver strong results across key plant KPIs, including safety, quality, food safety, cost, and service.
* Innovation & Project Execution: Lead the excellent execution of innovation and projects entering the plant, ensuring effective planning, cross-functional alignment, and successful implementation.
* Budgeting & Planning: Own the business planning and budgeting process for assigned units, including cost containment and resource allocation.
* Lean & CI Deployment: Champion and sustain lean manufacturing principles and WK Kellogg Integrated Work Systems (KIWS) across all units.
* Culture & Engagement: Drive a culture of safety, accountability, and engagement, promoting continuous learning and recognition.
* Compliance & Standards: Ensure compliance with all regulatory and internal standards related to safety, food safety, sanitation, and labor relations.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with support functions and external stakeholders to optimize performance and resolve complex challenges.

**Work Environment**

* This role is based within a 24/7 union manufacturing facility.
* Must be flexible to work any shift and travel up to 25%
* Regular presence on the production floor required
* Frequent interaction with internal teams and external partners

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required
* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing
* Proven success in leading large teams and managing multiple production lines
* Strong understanding of lean manufacturing and continuous improvement systems
* Demonstrated ability to lead through others and build effective teams
* Excellent strategic thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills
* Experience in union environments preferred
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office and SAP
* Experience with budget creation and performance management
* Experience working within a 24/7 manufacturing environment is preferred

***Salary Range:***

*$164,160 - $205,200*
*Salary pay ranges are determined by role and level. Within the range, the successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on factors including job-related skills, experience, certifications, qualifications, relevant education or training, and local market conditions.*
*At WK Kellogg Co, our success depends on our most vital asset — our people. That’s why we’re committed to providing you with benefits and programs that support your Total Health and your journey to be and feel your best — physically, financially, emotionally, and socially.*
*Although subject to change, the below are the benefits currently offered in association with this position:*

* Incentive Plan bonus eligibility
* Health, dental and vision insurance
* Savings and Investment Plan with Company match and contribution
* Paid Time Off (includes paid sick time)
* 11 Paid Holidays
* Life Insurance, AD and D Insurance and STD/LTD
* Tuition reimbursement, adoption assistance for eligible employees
* Employee recognition program

*The above offerings are subject to the terms of WKKC policies, which will control in the event of a conflict with the above descriptions*
*Our comprehensive and competitive benefits not only deliver value to you and your family, but also offer choice to meet your unique needs and knowledge to empower confident decision-making.*
**About Wk Kellogg Co**
*At WK Kellogg Co, we bring our best to everyone, every day through our trusted foods and brands. Our journey began in 1894, when our founder W.K. Kellogg reimagined the future of food with the creation of Corn Flakes, changing breakfast forever. Since then, we have embraced the same spirit of innovation and entrepreneurship in everything we do, channeling our founder’s passion and commitment to creating high quality and delicious products while fostering communities. Our iconic brand portfolio includes Frosted Flakes, Rice Krispies, Froot Loops, Kashi, Special K, Raisin Bran, Frosted Mini Wheats, and Bear Naked. With a presence in the majority of households across North America, our brands play a key role in enhancing the lives of millions of consumers every day, promoting a strong sense of physical, emotional and societal wellbeing. Our beloved brand characters, including Tony the Tiger and Toucan Sam, represent our deep connections with the consumers and communities we serve. For more information, visit*
*www.wkkellogg.com*
*.*

*If we can help you with a reasonable accommodation throughout the application or hiring process, please email TalentAssist@wkkellogg.com*
***THE FINER PRINT***
*The ability to work a full shift, come to work on time, work overtime as needed and the ability to work according to the necessary schedule to meet job requirements with or without reasonable accommodation is an essential function of this position.*
*WK Kellogg Co is an Equal Opportunity Employer that strives to provide an inclusive work environment, a seat for everyone at the table, and embraces the diverse talent of its people. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, ethnicity, disability, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, sexual orientation, age, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.*
**For US Applicants**

new_roles.title: Senior Manager of Operations
new_roles.description:
**Senior Manager of Operations - Austin, TX**

**DESCRIPTION:**

We’re seeking a hands-on Sr. Operations Manager with experience scaling silicon-based products in a semiconductor company. This player-coach role owns the operational path from foundry and wafer production through test, backend processing, and manufacturing. You’ll qualify and manage manufacturing vendors, establish and strengthen quality-control measures, and drive consistent quality, yield, cost, and delivery as production grows.

Experience with RFID inlay production is especially relevant.

**What you’ll do:**

* Own foundry relationships from negotiation through production execution, and scale wafer level production.
* Manage wafer-test facility relationships; evaluate and qualify test partners, and select test equipment to optimize cost, quality, and throughput.
* Lead test development, wafer backend operations, yield improvement, reliability, and failure analysis.
* Qualify and manage manufacturing vendors, including overseeing end-to-end inlay production and its ramp to volume.
* Establish and improve quality-control measures, operating procedures, and RMA processes.
* Monitor supplier quality, conduct supply-chain audits, and resolve manufacturing, quality, and delivery issues.
* Establish and improve ERP/MRP processes, WIP tracking, inventory planning, and production controls.
* Develop cost models, negotiate contracts, and drive improvements in cost, quality, and delivery.
* Manage one direct report and coordinate work across four internal engineers and executive stakeholders, including the CEO.

**What you’ll bring:**

* BSEE or equivalent practical experience.
* 7–10 years of operations, manufacturing, or related experience in a semiconductor company.
* Experience with RFID inlay manufacturing is a plus.
* Hands-on experience with silicon-based products and semiconductor manufacturing operations.
* Experience scaling products from wafer fabrication and test through backend processing and volume production.
* Experience working with foundries, wafer-test facilities, and manufacturing vendors.
* Familiarity with yield optimization, reliability, quality assurance, supplier audits, failure analysis, ERP/MRP systems, WIP tracking, and inventory planning.
* Strong communication, coordination, and negotiation skills, with a practical, roll-up-your sleeves approach.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Asia Manufacturing Strategy & Operations
new_roles.description:
**Job Description Summary**
The Senior Manager, Global Innovation, oversees performance management, operational excellence, and strategic execution for manufacturing entities across Asia, including Vietnam, China, and South Korea. Serves as a key liaison between headquarters and regional production sites, driving data‑driven decision‑making, productivity improvements, and process standardization.
 
 
**Job Description**
**Key Responsibilities**

* Performance Management & Financial Oversight
* Monitor and evaluate the operational and financial performance of manufacturing subsidiaries in Asia
* Develop and manage KPIs
* Lead monthly and quarterly business reviews with regional leadership
* Identify performance gaps and implement corrective action plans
* Strategic Planning & Execution
* Formulate mid- to long-term manufacturing and supply chain strategies aligned with global business objectives
* Support capacity planning, cost optimization, and footprint strategy (e.g., China+1, nearshoring)
* Conduct market and operational feasibility analysis for new investments or expansions
* Operational Excellence & Process Improvement
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives across production sites (Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen)
* Standardize processes and implement best practices across regions
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams (Procurement, Logistics, Quality, R&D) to improve end-to-end efficiency
* HQ–Regional Coordination
* Act as the primary liaison between HQ and Asia manufacturing teams
* Ensure alignment on corporate policies, reporting standards, and operational priorities
* Facilitate communication, issue resolution, and project execution across time zones
* Data Analytics & Reporting
* Build and maintain dashboards and reporting systems for real-time performance tracking
* Analyze large datasets to generate actionable insights and executive-level reports
* Support digital transformation initiatives (ERP, MES, data integration)

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, or related field (MBA preferred)
* 7–10+ years of experience in manufacturing, supply chain, or operations strategy roles
* Proven experience managing or overseeing operations in Asia (Vietnam, China, Korea preferred)
* Strong analytical skills with proficiency in Excel, Power BI/Tableau, or similar tools
* Deep understanding of manufacturing KPIs and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma)
* Experience working in a global, matrixed organization

**Preferred Skills**

* Familiarity with ERP systems (SAP, Oracle, etc.)
* Multilingual capability (Korean, Chinese, or Vietnamese is a plus)
* Strong project management and stakeholder management skills
* Ability to travel internationally (20–40%)

**Benefits**

* Premium Medical Insurance Coverage
* 401(k) Savings Plan
* Paid Time Off (PTO) based on seniority
* Paid Holidays

**Additional Workplace Offerings (subject To Change Or Eligibility.)**

* Annual Bonus Plan
* Onsite Employee Fitness Center with Indoor Racquetball Court and Yoga Room
* Summer Fridays
* Complimentary Gourmet Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner
* Relocation Support for New Hires
* Work Anniversary Recognitions
* Congratulatory & Condolence Gifts
* Employee Referral Bonus Program
* License/Certification Reimbursements
* Corporate Employee Discounts
* Visa Sponsorships (100% paid by the company) i.e., New H-1B, H-1B Transfer, O-1, and Green Card
* Commuter Support (Shuttle Bus Program and EZPass Support)
* Vehicle Perks

**Qualification(s)**
**Education(s):**
Bachelor of Science (B.S) (Required)
 
 
**Work Experience**
Experience Range V: +13 years of relevant experience or industry exposure in a related field
 
 
**Skill(s)**
Lean Process Improvements, Manufacturing, Operational Strategies, Six Sigma Framework, Supply Chain
 
 
**Language(s)**
English, Korean
 
 
**Certification(s)**
Not Applicable
 
 
The anticipated compensation range is
 
 
91,000.00 - 172,000.00 USD Annual
 
 
Actual compensation will be determined based on various factors including qualifications, education, experience, and location. The pay range is subject to change at any time dependent on a variety of internal and external factors.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality Engineering - Manufacturing Operations (2nd Shift)
new_roles.description:
The
**Senior Manager, Quality Engineering (2nd Shift)**
is a people leadership and manufacturing quality role responsible for providing quality and compliance oversight across second-shift operations. This leader will manage and develop a team of Quality Engineers while partnering closely with Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Facilities, Maintenance, and Supply Chain to ensure manufacturing activities are performed safely, effectively, and in compliance with applicable quality system requirements.
 
 
The position will oversee quality and compliance activities supporting the plant’s major production areas, including THV manufacturing, TMTT manufacturing, advanced catheters, and metals. The successful candidate will strengthen NCR and CAPA execution, improve investigation quality, monitor operational quality metrics, and establish effective communication and continuity between first- and second-shift teams.
 
 
***This position supports our 2nd-shift operation (Monday - Thursday, 3:30 PM - 2:30 AM).***
**How You'll Make an Impact:**

* Lead, coach, and develop a team of Quality Engineers supporting second-shift manufacturing operations, establishing clear expectations, accountability, and individual development plans.
* Provide quality and compliance oversight for second-shift manufacturing activities, ensuring operations are performed in accordance with approved procedures, quality system requirements, and applicable regulatory standards.
* Oversee the initiation, investigation, review, approval, and timely closure of nonconformance reports, including evaluating investigation quality, root cause determination, corrective actions, and product or process risk.
* Own and provide leadership for CAPAs, including investigation strategy, root cause analysis, action planning, implementation, effectiveness verification, and sustainable closure.
* Lead the deployment, implementation, and continuous improvement of quality management systems and manufacturing quality processes aligned with ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820.
* Review and approve test method validations, measurement system analyses, and manufacturing process validations, including IQ, OQ, and PQ documentation.
* Monitor quality metrics, trends, investigation performance, and quality data reviews; identify emerging risks and provide actionable recommendations to Operations and Quality leadership.
* Support internal and external audits by ensuring second-shift operations remain inspection-ready, responding to auditor questions, and leading or supporting actions resulting from audit observations.
* Partner with Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Manufacturing, Facilities, Maintenance, and Supply Chain to resolve quality issues, maintain compliant production, and strengthen operational controls.
* Establish effective shift-to-shift communication and escalation processes to ensure timely transfer of quality, production, and compliance information.
* Provide quality leadership for supplier-related issues, as applicable, including investigation support, corrective actions, and supplier performance concerns.
* Promote a culture of quality, accountability, continuous improvement, and proactive risk management throughout second-shift operations.
* Develop and implement quality processes that improve product compliance, operational performance, and customer satisfaction.
* Other incidental duties as assigned.

**What You'll Need (Required):**

* Bachelor’s degree with relevant Quality Engineering, Quality Management, or Manufacturing Quality experience within a highly regulated environment; or equivalent experience based on Edwards’ criteria.
* Demonstrated people leadership experience managing and developing engineers or other technical quality professionals.
* Experience deploying, implementing, or sustaining quality management systems within a regulated manufacturing environment, including working knowledge of ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820 requirements.
* Strong experience leading CAPAs, nonconformance investigations, and structured root cause analysis, including evaluation of investigation quality and effectiveness.
* Ability to work onsite during the designated second-shift schedule, Monday through Thursday, 3:30 PM to 2:30 AM.

**What Else We Look For (Preferred):**

* Engineering or Scientific degree
* Medical device manufacturing experience
* Experience providing quality oversight for manufacturing or production operations, including partnering directly with Operations and Engineering to resolve compliance and product quality issues.
* Demonstrated ability to interpret quality data, monitor operational quality metrics, recognize adverse trends, and escalate significant risks.
* Experience with microbiology principles or microbiological controls in a regulated manufacturing environment.
* Experience supporting cleanroom qualification, environmental controls, or manufacturing operations performed within controlled environments.
* Supplier quality or supplier management experience, including supplier investigations and corrective actions.
* Experience reviewing or approving test method validations and measurement system analysis studies.
* Experience reviewing or approving manufacturing process validations, including IQ/OQ/PQ.
* Experience supporting internal, external, or regulatory audits.
* Experience leading quality activities across multiple manufacturing technologies, product lines, or production areas.
* Knowledge of statistical methods, process capability, measurement systems, risk management, and continuous improvement tools.
* Demonstrated success strengthening team capability, improving organizational effectiveness, and leading change within a manufacturing quality organization.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence decisions and communicate effectively across technical, operational, and leadership audiences.

new_roles.title: Senior Manager, Quality
new_roles.description:
**Work Schedule**
Standard (Mon-Fri)
 
 
**Environmental Conditions**
Office
 
 
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
 
 
**LOCATION**
: On-site Logan, UT.
 
 

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**POSITION SUMMARY:**
The Senior Manager, Quality for BEA and Flexible Operations at the Logan, Utah site is responsible for leading site quality operations and ensuring compliance, product quality, and continuous improvement across manufacturing processes supporting flexible single-use technologies and products. This role partners closely with Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, and site leadership to drive operational excellence, maintain regulatory compliance, and support business growth.
 
 
The Senior Manager, Quality will lead quality teams responsible for manufacturing quality, quality systems, and customer quality activities while fostering a strong culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and customer focus.
 
 
**WHAT YOU WILL DO:**
**Site Quality Leadership:**

* Lead and develop the site quality organization supporting BEA and Flexible Operations manufacturing activities.
* Establish and maintain a strong quality culture focused on compliance, operational excellence, and continuous improvement.
* Serve as a key member of the Logan site leadership team, contributing to strategic and operational decision-making.
* Drive accountability through quality metrics, performance management, and development planning.
* Mentor and coach quality leaders and team members to build organizational capability.

**Quality Systems:**

* Ensure site compliance with applicable global regulatory requirements, industry standards, and internal quality management systems.
* Maintain site inspection readiness, including support for customer, notified body, and regulatory agency audits.
* Oversee effectiveness of Flexible site quality systems including: CAPA, Change control, Nonconformance management, Complaint handling, Document control, Training compliance, Risk management and Validation activities
* Drive timely and effective investigations, root cause analysis and corrective actions.
* Support implementation and harmonization of divisional quality initiatives and procedures.

**Operational Quality Support:**

* Partner cross functionally to reduce cost of poor quality and improve operational efficiency.
* Utilize data analytics and quality metrics to identify trends, risks, and improvement opportunities.
* Support product transfers, capacity expansions, and new product introductions
* Ensure robust investigation practices and timely resolution of deviations and customer concerns.
* Build strong customer relationships through responsiveness, transparency, and quality performance.

**HOW YOU WILL GET HERE:**
**Education & Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Chemistry, Quality, or related technical discipline required
* Advanced degree preferred
* 8+ years of progressive quality experience within regulated manufacturing environments
* 3+ years of leadership experience managing quality teams
* Experience in medical device, bioprocessing, pharmaceutical, life sciences, or single-use manufacturing environments preferred
* Strong knowledge of quality systems and regulatory requirements including ISO 9001, ISO 13485, GMP, and FDA regulations

**Technical & Leadership Competencies:**

* Strong leadership and team development capabilities
* Proven ability to drive quality improvements in manufacturing environments
* Expertise in root cause analysis, CAPA, risk management, and quality systems
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills
* Ability to influence and build strong partnerships across functions
* Experience supporting audits and regulatory inspections
* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment

**Key Success Metrics:**

* Audit outcomes
* Reduction in nonconformance and quality events
* CAPA effectiveness and closure timeliness
* Customer complaint reduction and responsiveness
* Employee engagement and talent development
* Continuous improvement and cost reduction results

**Leadership Expectations:**

* Demonstrate integrity, accountability and customer focus
* Lead through collaboration, communication and empowerment
* Foster a culture of quality, safety and continuous improvement
* Operate effectively in a fast-paced, matrixed, global organization
* Displays the Thermo Fisher 4i values of Innovation, Integrity, Intensity and Involvement

**Travel Requirements:**

* Travel up to 10% as required for business support, training and collaboration across sites

We offer competitive remuneration, annual incentive plan bonus scheme, healthcare, company 401k, and a range of employee benefits! Thermo Fisher Scientific offers employment with an innovative, forward-thinking organization, and outstanding career and development prospects. We offer an exciting company culture that stands for integrity, intensity, involvement, and innovation.
 
 
Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, or any other legally protected status. We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided a reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform critical job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request an accommodation.
