Job details:
 
**Fast growing manufacturing organization adding to their leadership team!**
This Jobot Job is hosted by: Brandon Fobert
 
Are you a fit? Easy Apply now by clicking the "Easy Apply" button
 
and sending us your resume.
 
Salary: $130,000 - $150,000 per year
 
 
 
**A bit about us:**
Growing manufacturing organization!!
 
 
 
**Why join us?**
Full Benefits package for all employees that includes: Medical, Dental, Vision. Holidays and PTO offered as well.
 
 
 
**Job Details**
Director of Quality
 
 
ABOUT THE ROLE
 
Lead quality for a mission-critical manufacturing operation where product performance directly supports customer trust and mission success. As Director of Quality, you will strengthen quality systems, build high-performing teams, and ensure precision-manufactured products meet demanding customer and government requirements.
 
 
You will partner with Manufacturing, Engineering, Supply Chain, and executive leadership to drive reliable performance across weapons, defense contracting, aerospace, and other highly regulated programs. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone equally comfortable on the shop floor and in the boardroom.
 
 
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
 

* Lead the Quality organization, setting clear objectives, accountability, and a culture of continuous improvement
* Develop, implement, and maintain a Quality Management System that meets precision manufacturing, aerospace, defense, and government contracting requirements
* Translate customer specifications, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements into quality plans, inspection methods, and acceptance criteria
* Oversee incoming, in-process, and final inspection to verify conformity, documentation accuracy, and traceability
* Partner with Engineering and Production to prevent defects, improve process capability, and resolve quality challenges
* Direct root cause investigations, corrective and preventive actions, nonconformance management, and material review
* Serve as the primary quality contact for customers, suppliers, auditors, and government representatives
* Lead internal, customer, supplier, and third-party audits, ensuring timely closure of findings and sustained compliance
* Establish and monitor quality metrics, including defect rates, cost of poor quality, customer complaints, and corrective action effectiveness
* Strengthen supplier quality through qualification, assessment, and improvement initiatives
* Recruit, coach, and develop quality professionals while promoting rigorous inspection practices and sound decision-making
* Communicate quality risks, performance trends, and improvement priorities to executive leadership

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
 

* 7+ years of progressive quality experience in manufacturing, including leadership of quality teams, systems, or programs
* Experience in weapons manufacturing, defense contracting, aerospace, or another highly regulated precision manufacturing environment
* Strong knowledge of inspection practices, dimensional verification, engineering drawings, GD&T, and precision measurement equipment
* Experience implementing or maintaining a QMS aligned with ISO 9001, AS9100, or equivalent standards
* Working knowledge of government contracting quality obligations, contractual flow-down requirements, and compliance documentation
* Demonstrated success leading audits, resolving complex quality issues, and implementing sustainable corrective actions
* Proficiency in root cause analysis, statistical process control, risk assessment, and continuous improvement methodologies
* Strong leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the confidence to represent Quality in customer and executive discussions
* Bachelor's degree in engineering, quality, manufacturing, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
 

* Master's degree in engineering, quality, operations, or business administration
* ASQ CMQ/OE, CQE, ISO Lead Auditor, or Lean Six Sigma certification
* NADCAP experience, including Chemical Processing and Non-Destructive Testing
* Familiarity with AS9102 first article inspection, FAR/DFARS, and DCMA oversight

identity_held_roles.title: Director, Quality Assurance
identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Summary:**

The Director of Quality Assurance is a leadership role, responsible for all aspects of the Quality Systems, Clinical Quality and Manufacturing Quality for Aquestive. The Director of Quality Assurance will work with their direct managerial reports, as well as Executive Leadership, to ensure a continued state of compliance while promoting a strong quality culture across the organization for all products, spanning early phase development to commercialization.

This position will be expected to work in a highly collaborative, cross functional team environment, and provide expert knowledge to risk identification/mitigation, strategy and execution.

**Responsibilities:**

* Oversee all aspects of Quality Systems, Clinical Quality and Manufacturing Quality to assure compliance with FDA, EU, ANVISA, TGA and other international GMP requirements for all products manufactured at Aquestive (e.g., 21 CFR Part 210 + 211, EU GMP Volume 4 Part 1).
* Provide strategic direction and leadership to ensure effectiveness of Quality Systems (e.g., CAPA, Change Management, Event Management, Supplier Quality, Internal Audit, Document Management, Risk Management, Record Review and Product Disposition, Training, Field Alert/Recall, etc.)
* Lead and ensure execution of quality strategy for all development and manufacturing activities associated with all products manufactured by Aquestive, including external GMP contract manufacture operations or laboratories for drug substance and drug product.
* Primary contact for all inspection interactions with all domestic and ex-US regulatory authorities.
* Provide direction for escalated quality issues as they arise, determining the need for, and structuring communication for, further escalation to the Executive team and/or external parties.
* Lead strategic quality to quality relationships with business partners, suppliers, external CMOs and third-party testing laboratories.
* Ensure the company is upholding to Quality/Technical Agreements with business partners and suppliers.
* Provides input to all functions to ensure clinical trial activities are conducted in compliance with GCP regulations and internal requirements.
* Actively participate in the Site Leadership Team to drive continuous improvement activities and initiatives throughout Aquestive.
* Analyze, report and present metrics where applicable to show health of system(s).
* Lead GxP inspection strategies across all auditable areas to ensure the company is in an audit-ready status at all times.
* Manage overall coaching, training, development and succession planning for the function.
* Set, manage and monitor budget for Quality Assurance, in conjunction with finance.

**Qualifications:**

* Minimum of Bachelor’s degree required. Advanced degree in chemistry, engineering, biochemistry, or related science field desirable.
* Minimum 7+ years of related work experience working in a regulated GxP industry in pharmaceutical manufacturing operation setting or service oriented laboratory.
* Demonstrated ability to direct a function, oversee projects and teams. Minimum of 2 years overseeing direct reports.
* Minimum of 2+ years working in a managerial role with direct reports.
* Strong skillset in problem solving, strategic thinking, critical reasoning and decision making.
* Strong interpersonal skills and verbal/written communication skills.
* Excellent computer skills required (e.g., Microsoft Word, Excel, Access, PowerPoint, Visio).
* Strong project management skills, strong organizational skills to maintain a high level of productivity, innovation, and priority-setting to complete assignments on time and on budget.
* Strong business acumen surrounding pharmaceutical manufacturing.
* Some travel required.

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of the work being performed by colleagues assigned to this position. This is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required. Aquestive reserves the right to make changes to the job description whenever necessary.

As part of Aquestive’s employment process, final candidate will be required to complete a drug test and background check prior to employment commencing. 
**Please Note:**
Aquestive is a drug-free workplace and has a drug free workplace policy in place.

Aquestive provides equal employment opportunities to all colleagues and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.

The Company is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the salary range for this job in certain states and cities within the United States. Final determinations with respect to salary will take into account a number of factors, which may include, but not be limited to the primary work location and the chosen candidate’s relevant skills, experience, and education.

Equal Opportunity Employer
 
 
This employer is required to notify all applicants of their rights pursuant to federal employment laws.
 
For further information, please review the Know Your Rights notice from the Department of Labor.

identity_held_roles.title: VP, Regional Manufacturing
identity_held_roles.description:
**Overview**
Primo Brands is a leading branded beverage company in North America with a focus on healthy hydration. We are proud to offer an extensive and iconic portfolio of highly recognizable, sustainably sourced, and conveniently packaged branded beverages distributed across more than 150,000 retail outlets.
 
 
**Compensation:**
$185,048 - $248,596. This position is eligible for an annual bonus.
 
 
**Location:**
Dallas, TX
 
 
**Health Benefits**
Benefits of working for Primo Brands:
 
 
Medical, prescription, dental, vision, flexible spending account (FSA), dependent care flexible spending account (FSA), health savings account (HSA)
 
 
**Retirement/Investing**
401K with a 5% match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)
 
 
**Insurance**
Employee Life Insurance, short and long-term disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, spouse/domestic partner/child life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment
 
 
**Other Great Benefits**
Employee discounts, save on auto, home, and pet insurance, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation and sick time, 9 paid holidays and 3 paid floating holidays, paid leave for when you have a baby, adopt a child, or become a foster parent, legal services, identity theft protection, employee assistance program (EAP), adoption reimbursement benefit, FEDlogic, commuter benefits.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
The Regional Vice President (RVP), Manufacturing is responsible for leading the end-to-end manufacturing operations across a multi-site regional network within Primo Brands. This executive leader drives safety, quality, production, cost, service, people, and continuous improvement performance across factories while ensuring alignment with enterprise Supply Chain strategies and business objectives.
 
 
The RVP, Manufacturing partners closely with Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, Procurement, Planning, HR, and Finance leaders to deliver operational excellence, optimize manufacturing capacity, develop organizational capability, and support long-term business growth. The role is accountable for creating a high-performance culture that prioritizes safety, quality, associate engagement, customer service, and productivity improvements.
 
 
The Regional Vice President, Manufacturing reports to the Senior Vice President, Manufacturing Operations.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
**Safety & Compliance Leadership**

* Lead a culture where safety is the first priority and operational decisions reflect a zero-harm mindset.
* Ensure compliance with all federal, state, provincial, environmental, food safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Drive accountability for safety performance, incident reduction, risk mitigation, and compliance excellence.
* Serve as a visible champion for workplace safety and associate well-being.

**Manufacturing Operations**

* Lead manufacturing performance across multiple factories, ensuring consistent execution against operational objectives.
* Deliver production plans that support customer demand, service expectations, and inventory requirements.
* Drive schedule attainment, throughput, asset utilization, and manufacturing reliability.
* Optimize regional manufacturing capacity and network performance.
* Ensure disciplined execution of daily management systems and operational governance routines.

**Food Safety & Quality**

* Champion food safety and quality excellence across all facilities.
* Ensure manufacturing sites maintain compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, and company standards.
* Provide leadership oversight of quality management systems, audits, inspections, recalls, and corrective action processes.
* Promote a culture of first-time-right execution and continuous quality improvement.

**Financial & Productivity Performance**

* Own regional manufacturing budgets, labor productivity, conversion costs, and operating performance.
* Deliver annual productivity, cost savings, and efficiency targets.
* Identify opportunities to reduce waste, improve OEE, optimize labor deployment, and improve asset performance.
* Partner with Finance to ensure operational results support annual business plans and long-range objectives.

**Talent & Organizational Leadership**

* Build and lead high-performing teams through effective leadership, coaching, succession planning, and talent development.
* Develop strong Plant Directors, Factory Managers, Technical Managers, Operations Managers, and functional leaders.
* Drive leadership capability, workforce planning, succession readiness, and organizational effectiveness.
* Foster a culture of accountability, inclusion, collaboration, and associate engagement.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Lead implementation of manufacturing excellence initiatives across the region.
* Drive improvements in OEE, asset reliability, labor productivity, quality, and service performance.
* Leverage Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, TPM, and continuous improvement methodologies to drive sustainable results.
* Establish performance metrics and governance processes that accelerate operational excellence.

**Strategic Leadership**

* Contribute to the development and execution of Supply Chain and Manufacturing strategies.
* Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to evaluate network optimization opportunities, capacity investments, automation initiatives, and capital projects.
* Lead manufacturing integration, transformation, and change management initiatives.
* Support enterprise growth through scalable operational solutions and disciplined execution.

**Scope of Responsibility**

* Multiple manufacturing facilities within assigned region.
* Direct leadership of Plant Directors, Factory Managers, Regional Engineering, Manufacturing Excellence, and operational support functions.
* Accountability for regional safety, quality, production, service, cost, talent, and financial performance.
* Significant influence on capital planning, organizational design, and operational strategy.

**Qualifications**
**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business, or related field required.
* Master's Degree (MBA or related discipline) preferred.

**Experience**

* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 10+ years leading multi-site manufacturing operations.
* Experience managing large-scale manufacturing networks in food, beverage, consumer packaged goods, or related industries.
* Proven success leading large teams through operational transformation and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience managing significant P&L, productivity, and capital investment responsibilities.

**Skills & Competencies**

* Executive leadership and influence.
* Manufacturing operations expertise.
* Safety and quality systems leadership.
* Financial and operational acumen.
* Strategic thinking and execution.
* Change leadership and organizational transformation.
* Talent development and succession management.
* Data-driven decision making.
* Cross-functional collaboration.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

**Success Measures**

* Safety Performance
* Quality Compliance & Customer Metrics
* OEE and Asset Reliability
* Production Attainment
* Cost per Case Equivalent
* Labor Productivity
* Service Levels / OTIF
* Associate Engagement
* Leadership Bench Strength
* Productivity Savings Delivery
* Capital Project Execution
* Manufacturing Excellence Maturity

**If you're ready to embark on an exciting journey with Primo Brands, apply now!**
**Salary Range Disclaimer**
The salary range provided for this position is an approximation based on market research, internal compensation data and the candidate’s qualifications and experience. Final salary offers are determined through a comprehensive evaluation of candidate qualifications and may vary depending on factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location of the position. Other components of the compensation package, including benefits and bonuses, will also be considered. We are committed to fair and equitable compensation practices, and we encourage open dialogue about compensation during the interview process.
 
 
Primo Brands’ established portfolio includes billion-dollar brands Poland Spring® and Pure Life®, premium brands like Saratoga® and Mountain Valley®, regional leaders such as Arrowhead®, Deer Park®, Ice Mountain® Ozarka®, and Zephyrhills®, purified brands, Primo Water® and Sparkletts®, and flavored and enhanced brands like Splash® and AC+ION®. Our extensive direct-to-consumer offerings and industry-leading line-up of innovative water dispensers create consumer connectivity through recurring water purchases across Water Direct, Water Exchange, and Water Refill. At Primo Brands, our more than 11,000 associates are at the heart of what we do and deliver on our mission to provide healthy hydration to consumers wherever, however and whenever they want it. We believe in fostering a respectful culture, which values our associates who are deeply invested in quality hydration, our communities, and the sustainability of our packaging and water sources for generations to come.
 
 
Primo Brands is proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law.
 
 
Candidates must possess strong English language skills to effectively communicate with customers and provide exceptional service. Proficiency in English is essential for understanding customer needs, resolving inquiries, and collaborating with team members.

identity_held_roles.description:
Our client is a leading precision metal component manufacturer serving the automotive and industrial sectors. Operating multiple advanced manufacturing facilities across the United States, they specialize in high-volume production using advanced metal forming and stamping technologies. They supply critical components to tier-one automotive suppliers and industrial OEMs.

**The Role**

We are recruiting a Vice President of Manufacturing to lead manufacturing operations for a multi-facility U.S. operation. Reporting directly to the President, this role has responsibility for all manufacturing and quality departments at the primary facility and oversight of operations at additional locations. identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Title:**
Director of Operations / Director of Manufacturing / Plant Manager
**Location:**
Memphis, TN
**Department:**
Operations
**Reports To:**
CEO / COO
 
 
**Position Summary**
Vanguard Soap is seeking a strategic and hands-on Director of Operations (Plant Manager) to lead end-to-end manufacturing operations across liquid and solid soap production. This role is responsible for delivering operational excellence at scale, ensuring world-class quality, cost efficiency, production reliability, and safety performance.
 
 
This leader will translate business strategy into execution through disciplined manufacturing systems, strong people leadership, and continuous improvement. The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise, operational rigor, and a builder's mindset, capable of scaling a high-growth, entrepreneurial manufacturing environment into a best-in-class operation.
 
 
The Vanguard manufacturing campus is a 14-acre site producing 40-50 million pounds of product annually with over 100 employees.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
**Ensure Quality (Product Integrity & Compliance)**

* Establish and enforce world-class quality standards across all production lines, ensuring consistent product integrity and customer satisfaction
* Partner closely with Quality and Regulatory teams to ensure compliance with GMP, ISO, FDA, and customer-specific standards
* Implement robust quality systems, including in-process controls, root cause analysis, and corrective/preventive actions (CAPA)
* Drive a culture of "quality at the source," embedding accountability at every level of the organization
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives to reduce defects, waste, and rework

**Standardize Costs (Operational Efficiency & Margin Expansion)**

* Own plant-level cost structure, including labor, materials, yield, and overhead performance
* Identify and execute cost optimization initiatives through lean manufacturing, process engineering, and waste elimination
* Improve production yields, line efficiencies, and asset utilization across all manufacturing processes
* Develop and implement standardized operating procedures (SOPs) to ensure repeatability and cost discipline
* Partner with Finance and Supply Chain to align production planning with cost targets and margin goals

**Achieve Schedule (Delivery & Throughput Reliability)**

* Ensure on-time, in-full (OTIF) production performance aligned with customer commitments and business priorities
* Lead integrated production planning in partnership with Supply Chain, Procurement, and Customer teams
* Optimize production scheduling, capacity planning, and labor allocation across multiple product lines and shifts
* Proactively identify and resolve bottlenecks, downtime risks, and supply constraints
* Establish performance metrics and dashboards to drive accountability for throughput, uptime, and delivery performance

**Ensure Safety (People & Environmental Safety)**

* Champion a zero-incident safety culture, ensuring compliance with all OSHA and environmental regulations
* Establish and enforce safety policies, procedures, and training programs across the plant
* Lead safety audits, risk assessments, and incident investigations with a focus on prevention
* Ensure safe operation of all equipment, processes, and facility infrastructure
* Build a culture where safety is a core value and embedded in daily behaviors

**Enterprise & Leadership Responsibilities**

* Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing operations team, including Production, Maintenance, Engineering, and Supervisory leadership
* Build organizational capability to scale with company growth, including succession planning and talent development
* Drive a culture of accountability, performance management, and continuous improvement
* Lead capital investment planning, including equipment upgrades, automation, and facility expansion
* Serve as a key member of the leadership team, contributing to overall business strategy and execution
* Ensure alignment across Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, and Commercial teams

**Key Capabilities**

* Operational Leadership at Scale: Proven ability to lead full plant operations with accountability for safety, quality, cost, and delivery
* Continuous Improvement Mindset: Deep expertise in Lean, Six Sigma, and manufacturing excellence methodologies
* Technical & Engineering Acumen: Strong understanding of process engineering, equipment optimization, and manufacturing systems
* People Leadership & Team Building: Ability to attract, develop, and retain top talent while building a high-performance culture
* Execution Discipline: Translates strategy into clear priorities, metrics, and results
* Managing Complexity: Effectively balances multiple product lines, customer demands, and operational constraints
* Business & Financial Acumen: Understands cost drivers, margin levers, and operational impact on P&L performance

**Qualifications**

* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing operations
* Prior experience as a Plant Manager, Director of Operations, or Director of Manufacturing
* Experience in personal care, chemical, CPG, or contract manufacturing strongly preferred
* Demonstrated success driving improvements in safety, quality, cost, and delivery metrics
* Experience leading multi-shift operations and scaling manufacturing capabilities in a growth environment
* Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Chemical, Mechanical, Industrial, or related field required)
* Advanced degree (MBA or Master's in Engineering/Operations) preferred

**Additional Requirements**

* Strong knowledge of GMP, FDA, OSHA, and relevant regulatory standards
* Proven track record of implementing lean manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives
* Excellent leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills
* Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment with evolving priorities

identity_held_roles.description:
***Custom Fabrication & Assembly Manufacturing | Southeast Alabama***
**Location:**
Dothan, AL (Onsite).
*Relocation assistance is available.*
**Compensation:**
$165,000 to $180,000 base, plus 10% annual bonus
 
 
**Reports to:**
President, Signage Division
 
 
**Team:**
Top leader on site for a custom manufacturing facility with approximately 125 employees across welding, metal fabrication, CNC, forming, electrical, and assembly
 
 
**Required**

* 7+ years of hands-on manufacturing leadership experience with direct responsibility for plant-level performance, whether as a Director of Manufacturing, Plant Manager, Operations Manager, or similar role
* Experience leading a labor-intensive, high-mix, low-volume operation such as a job shop, fabrication, or build-to-order environment. Broad manufacturing judgment matters more than deep expertise in any single process
* A track record of improving throughput, labor efficiency, quality, and on-time delivery through steady, practical improvements while keeping production running
* Working knowledge of manufacturing cost, including labor standards, earned hours or standard costing, and how floor performance shows up in a plant P&L
* Strong floor presence and the ability to earn trust with a long-tenured workforce, build real buy-in, and hold people accountable when the reasons for falling short do not add up
* Experience building repeatable systems and a leadership structure that keep a plant running dependably without relying on any one person
* Resourcefulness and comfort delivering results in a lean environment without large corporate engineering or support teams behind you
* Clear, professional communication with executive and finance leadership, including regular reporting on plant performance
* Bachelor's degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent hands-on manufacturing experience will be considered
* Genuine comfort relocating to and leading in a small Southern community

**Nice to Have**

* Background in custom fabricated products such as signage, store fixtures, displays, architectural metals, or electrical closures
* Industrial engineering training or a similarly technical, process-focused background
* Experience in a private equity-backed or recently acquired manufacturing business
* Lean, Six Sigma, or similar continuous improvement experience applied in a practical, hands-on way
* Experience scaling production capacity, including adding shifts or growing output in a constrained labor market

**The Opportunity**
Our client is a private equity-backed national company that designs, builds, and installs branded products for well-known multi-site businesses across North America. This role leads their primary manufacturing facility in Southeast Alabama, a custom, build-to-order operation where a skilled team works hands-on with aluminum, steel, and electrical components, producing a wide variety of products in small lots.
 
 
The plant has made steady progress in recent years, with lower costs, better quality, and more reliable delivery. The next step is a strong, hands-on leader who can keep that momentum going and take the operation further. This is not a turnaround and not a maintenance role. It is a long-term opportunity to increase output, keep improving cost and efficiency, and build an operation that runs dependably every day.
 
 
**What You'll Do**

* Own plant performance: Lead every aspect of the facility, including safety, quality, throughput, delivery, and cost, with accountability for the plant P&L.
* Lead from the floor: Spend a good part of every day in production, getting to know the people, understanding what drives them, and building the trust that makes change stick.
* Find early wins: In the first 90 days, learn how the factory runs, stabilize performance, and identify practical process changes that make work easier for the people on the floor.
* Drive throughput and cost: Partner with the division President and finance leadership on a multi-year plan to increase output and reduce manufacturing cost, then deliver against it.
* Build repeatable systems: Put processes, metrics, and a leadership structure in place that let the plant run reliably without intensive oversight or dependence on any single person.
* Develop the team: Coach and grow the existing leadership group, including long-tenured leaders who know the product inside and out, and shape the structure the plant needs going forward.
* Hold the line on accountability: Understand the work well enough to see past excuses, set clear expectations, and follow through consistently.

**Why This Role Is Different**
This is the top leadership seat on site. The division President is based in another state, so this person will have real ownership and autonomy over how the plant runs, along with a leadership team that is invested in their success and has done this job before.
 
 
You will not be starting from scratch. The plant has a solid foundation, a clear direction, and the backing of a growing national platform and patient, long-term ownership. The opportunity is to take what has been built and make it better, with room to put your own mark on the operation.
 
 
**The Culture**
The plant has a loyal, tenured workforce that wants to do good work and takes pride in what it builds. The right person brings both process discipline and genuine people skills, someone who can hold the team to a high standard while building the relationships that earn real buy-in. Leadership is not looking for someone to shut things down and start over. They want a steady, visible leader who can find improvements while the work keeps moving, and who will feel at home in a close-knit, small-town Southern community.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Director of Manufacturing (Rubber)**

The Director of Manufacturing will oversee rubber production operations across 2 manufacturing plants with 200 total employees, 100 employees per plant, 1 union plant & 1 non-union, 5-8 Direct Reports (Department Managers) with responsibility for safety, quality, delivery, and cost, acting as leader with accountability for both operations.

**Location**
: Columbia, Missouri (Relocation Assistance Offered)

**Compensation**
: $175,000 - $215,000 base salary + 15% bonus.

**Benefits**
: Medical, Dental, Vision, STD, LTD, 401k Match 6%, 3 weeks PTO, Tuition Assistance, etc.

**Job Description:**

*Operational Leadership & Plant Management*

* Hold full P&L, safety, quality, delivery, and cost accountability for both rubber manufacturing plants across textile & milling operations including mixing and cord production, acting as a multi-site operations leader.
* Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team of 6-8 managers who in turn lead roughly 200 salaried and hourly employees across multiple shifts.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, capital plans, and budgets; manage conversion cost, yield, scrap, rework, material variance, and overhead against targets.
* Balance production schedules and capacity across both sites to meet downstream Belt and Hose demand, optimizing changeovers, inventory, and material availability.
* Partner with the VP of Manufacturing, plant managers of downstream operations, supply chain, and commercial teams on demand planning, capacity strategy, and make-versus-buy decisions.
* Spend meaningful time on the floor at each site (approximately 30% travel), maintaining a visible presence on all shifts and engaging directly with operators and supervisors.

*Compound Quality, Technology & Process Control*

* Own end-to-end compound consistency, using rheology (Mooney, MDR/RPA), physical properties, and downstream processing and molding results as the measures of success.
* Reduce process variation through structured methods such as design of experiments (DOE), statistical process control, capability studies, and root cause analysis.
* Develop, standardize, and improve mixing programs (load order, ram pressure, rotor speed, mix time, dump temperature, energy-based and multi-stage mixing) for new and existing compounds, including EPDM, CR, HNBR, NBR, SBR, and NR systems.
* Oversee textile operations (cord unwinding, coating, and rewinding) and raw material handling, heating, and cooling to ensure consistent adhesion and reinforcement performance in finished belts and hoses.
* Lead cross-functional troubleshooting with chemists, the materials lab, process and manufacturing engineers, and downstream operations, leading investigations through disciplined experimentation.
* Establish a single, controlled system of work instructions, batch cards, and process parameters across both sites so that the same compound is produced the same way regardless of site, shift, or operator.
* Evaluate and recommend mixing equipment, automation, weighing/batching, and tooling options for current and new processes and products.

Mill: raw materials are received and handled, then weighed, mixed, heated, and cooled to produce uniform rubber compound for downstream product production.

Textiles: cord is carefully unwound, coated, and rewound to specification, giving finished products consistent strength and adhesion.

*Safety, Compliance & Culture*

* Champion a zero-harm safety culture, including lockout/tagout, machine guarding, mill nip and pinch-point hazards, hot surfaces, combustible dust, and chemical handling.
* Ensure compliance with OSHA, EPA, environmental permitting, SDS requirements, and applicable customer, ISO/IATF, and corporate standards.
* Drive 5S, standardized work, and lean manufacturing practices; treat housekeeping as both a safety and a quality requirement.
* Build a culture of accountability in which following the documented process is the standard and deviations are surfaced openly.

*Talent Development & Organizational Capability*

* Build a bench of operators, leads, supervisors, and managers through structured training, skills matrices, cross-training, and succession planning.
* Set clear expectations, conduct performance reviews, and partner with HR on coaching, corrective action, recognition, and labor relations.
* Capture experienced operators' tribal knowledge and convert it to documented, teachable standards.
* Attract, hire, and retain top technical and operational talent in a competitive labor market.

*Strategy & Continuous Improvement*

* Work with the plant leadership and engineering leadership to define annual improvement initiatives, then align cross-functional teams to targets and track results.
* Lead capital projects, technology transfers, and new-process launches from concept through ramp-up.
* Use KPIs, trend charts, and daily management routines to drive visibility, problem solving, and sustained results.
* Contribute to the North American and global compounding strategy, sharing best practices with sister sites and corporate technology teams.

*Key Performance Indicators*

* Safety: recordable incident rate, near-miss reporting, and audit results
* Compound first-pass quality and out-of-spec rate; rheology capability and variation reduction
* Downstream molding and processing results attributable to compound and cord
* Schedule attainment and on-time delivery to downstream operations
* Scrap, rework, yield, and material and conversion cost versus budget
* Equipment uptime and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)
* Operator qualification coverage and cross-training depth
* Employee engagement, turnover, and leadership bench strength

**Qualifications Seeking:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering (Chemical, Polymer, Mechanical, Materials, or Industrial), Chemistry, or a related technical field preferred. Experience in lieu of Bachelors will be considered.
* 8+ years of manufacturing experience, including 5–10 years of hands-on polymer or rubber compounding and mixing experience.
* 5+ years of progressive leadership experience managing managers and multi-shift operations, including responsibility for safety, quality, cost, and delivery.
* Strong working knowledge of internal mixers (tangential and intermeshing), two-roll mills, TSE, weigh-up/batching, and compound testing (Mooney, MDR/RPA, specific gravity, dispersion).
* Demonstrated experience reducing process variation using DOE, SPC, and structured problem-solving methods.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional troubleshooting with chemists, lab, engineering, and production teams.
* Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, direct without being abrasive.
* Willingness and ability to travel approximately 30% between sites and to work on the floor in a manufacturing environment.

**Preferred Qualifications (Not Required):**

* Master's degree in Polymer Science, Chemistry, or Engineering, or an MBA.
* Experience in belt, hose, or other engineered rubber product manufacturing, with understanding of rheology and downstream extrusion, calendering, and molding.
* Experience with cord treatment, textile reinforcement, or adhesive systems.
* Experience managing multi-site operations and leading change across sites.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Green Belt certification, or equivalent.
* Familiarity with ERP/MES systems, mixing control software, and automation for production and material traceability.
* Experience leading capital projects, new-equipment commissioning, or greenfield/expansion launches.

**Core Competencies Seeking:**

* Technical depth: credible expert in rubber chemistry, rheology, and mixing who can coach engineers and operators alike.
* Leadership: develops managers, builds accountability, and engages a unionized or non-union frontline workforce.
* Systems thinking: standardizes work and builds sustainable processes rather than relying on individual heroics.
* Analytical rigor: makes decisions with data, experimentation, and clear trend visibility.
* Business acumen: manages cost, capital, and capacity with a P&L mindset.
* Learning agility: quickly learns new technologies and applies them to business needs.

**About the Opportunity**

A well-established manufacturing organization in the aviation and aerospace industry is seeking an experienced
**Director of Production**
to oversee and improve its manufacturing operations.

This is a hands-on leadership opportunity for someone with direct aerospace or aviation manufacturing experience who can manage production activities, lead teams, improve operational efficiency, and ensure consistent product quality and on-time delivery.

The ideal candidate is a practical, floor-oriented leader who understands production planning, manufacturing processes, equipment maintenance, and resource management.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Oversee daily manufacturing and production activities to ensure operational efficiency, product quality, and timely delivery.
* Manage production schedules, workflow, resource allocation, and manufacturing capacity.
* Lead and coordinate production planning and maintenance teams to maintain equipment reliability and operational continuity.
* Monitor production costs, operating expenses, and departmental budgets while identifying cost-saving opportunities.
* Establish and track KPIs related to productivity, production volume, quality, scrap rates, lead times, and on-time delivery.
* Identify opportunities to improve manufacturing processes, reduce waste, and increase production capacity.
* Ensure compliance with aviation manufacturing standards, safety regulations, environmental requirements, and customer specifications.
* Work closely with department managers and supervisors to establish performance goals and maintain accountability.
* Coach, develop, and mentor production leaders and supervisors.
* Support facility improvements, equipment upgrades, capital projects, and the implementation of new manufacturing technologies.
* Promote a culture of continuous improvement, teamwork, safety, and operational excellence.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field; equivalent experience will also be considered.
* Approximately 8–10 years of progressive leadership experience in a manufacturing environment.
* Direct experience in
 **aviation or aerospace manufacturing operations is required**
 .
* Previous experience managing production teams, manufacturing schedules, and operational resources.
* Strong understanding of production planning, manufacturing processes, maintenance coordination, and quality control.
* Experience with Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Demonstrated ability to improve productivity, control costs, and meet production targets.
* Strong leadership, problem-solving, organizational, and decision-making skills.
* **Fluency in both English and Spanish (written and spoken) is required.**

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience working with ERP systems; Quantum experience is a plus.
* Six Sigma Green Belt certification or higher.
* Lean Manufacturing or other continuous improvement certifications.
* Experience managing manufacturing budgets and operational performance metrics.

**Ideal Candidate**

The successful candidate will be a hands-on production leader who is comfortable working directly with manufacturing teams and supervisors. This position is best suited for someone with a strong background in aerospace manufacturing who can balance people leadership with daily production execution and continuous improvement.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Description**
As the Fort Wayne OEM Director of Manufacturing, you will be a key leadership contributor to the success of the Fort Wayne Manufacturing Hub. Reporting to the Hub Director of Manufacturing, you will provide inspirational leadership in a rapidly growing business and have responsibility for all original equipment manufacturing at the site. This role demands a strategic, results-oriented leader with a proven track record of building and scaling rapidly growing organizations. Because of the need for consistent, in-person collaboration and/or the requirement to perform all work onsite due to the nature of this particular role, it will be performed full-time on site. This means work will be conducted on location at a BAE Systems facility 100% of the time.
 
 
 
 
**Key Responsibilities Include**
**Strategic Product Stream Leadership**

* Own the strategic direction, execution, and performance of the Circuit Card Assembly and Unit Integration factories
* Serve as the primary point of contact between production and program management

**Program Execution**

* Oversee execution of manufacturing in alignment with program schedules
* Ensure all contractual obligations (cost, schedule, performance) are met or exceeded

**Performance Improvement**

* Drive continuous improvement using Lean, Six Sigma Principles
* Implement metrics to monitor production performance
* Initiate corrective actions to resolve production variances, quality escapes, and manufacturing cost variances

**Required Education, Experience, & Skills**

* Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Industrial Technology, Operations Management, or related field; equivalent experience considered OR 20 years manufacturing experience with no degree
* Minimum 10 years’ experience in production/manufacturing
* Minimum 6 years’ experience leading production/manufacturing teams including managing people leaders
* Proficiency with manufacturing management concepts
* Proficiency applying Lean Manufacturing principles and visual management tools

**Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills**

* Proficiency with Oracle ERP
* Formal Lean or Six Sigma training/certification
* Minimum 10 years’ experience leading people leaders of production/manufacturing teams

**Pay Information**
Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743
 
 
Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.
 
 
Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.
 
 
 
 
**About BAE Systems, Inc.**
BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.
 
 
Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. We're developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you're not just building a career. You're contributing to a mission that truly matters.
 
 
This position will be posted for at least 5 calendar days. The posting will remain active until the position is filled, or a qualified pool of candidates is identified.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Description**
Executive Manufacturing Leadership Opportunity
 
 
BASX is seeking a transformational manufacturing executive to lead one of its key operations as Site Leader (Director of Manufacturing).
 
 
This role is far more than manufacturing oversight. It is an opportunity to shape the future of a growing operation, influence enterprise strategy, drive large-scale operational transformation, and build the manufacturing capabilities required to support long-term business growth.
 
 
As the senior manufacturing leader for the site, you will serve as a trusted business partner to executive leadership and will be responsible for aligning manufacturing strategy, operational performance, capital investment, workforce development, and technology advancement with the organization's strategic objectives.
 
 
The successful candidate will bring a balance of strategic vision and operational discipline while building a culture of accountability, innovation, continuous improvement, and sustainable growth.
 
 
**This Is a Unique Opportunity To**




+ Lead manufacturing operations that directly support the growth strategy of a rapidly expanding organization.
+ Shape the future-state manufacturing vision through automation, digital transformation, and Industry 4.0 initiatives.
+ Influence major capital investment decisions, facility expansion plans, and manufacturing technology roadmaps.
+ Build leadership capability and strengthen organizational effectiveness across the operation.
+ Partner directly with executive leadership to establish long-term operational strategies.
+ Drive measurable improvements in productivity, quality, safety, delivery performance, and profitability.
+ Leave a lasting legacy by creating a scalable manufacturing organization positioned for future growth.

**What You'll Accomplish**
**Enterprise Impact**




+ Establish and execute a multi-year manufacturing strategy aligned with company growth initiatives.
+ Lead initiatives that enhance operational scalability, profitability, and customer satisfaction.
+ Drive business performance through operational excellence, capacity optimization, and strategic planning.

**Manufacturing Transformation**




+ Lead cultural and operational transformation initiatives across the facility.
+ Advance Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement principles throughout the organization.
+ Champion automation, smart factory technologies, and digital manufacturing capabilities.
+ Identify and implement breakthrough improvements that create sustainable competitive advantages.

**Executive Partnership**




+ Serve as a key member of the site leadership team.
+ Collaborate with executive leadership on strategic business decisions.
+ Influence organizational direction through data-driven decision-making and operational expertise.
+ Provide strategic recommendations regarding investments, growth opportunities, risk mitigation, and resource allocation.

**Leadership Development**




+ Build and mentor a high-performing leadership team.
+ Create succession plans and strengthen organizational capability.
+ Foster a culture focused on accountability, engagement, innovation, and results.
+ Attract and retain top manufacturing talent.

**Scope & Organizational Impact**
Serves as the senior manufacturing leader for BASX's Redmond operation, directing a workforce of more than 500 employees across a manufacturing footprint exceeding 300,000 square feet. Responsible for shaping manufacturing strategy, leading operational transformation, guiding capital investments, and building the organizational capabilities required to support continued growth and market leadership.
 
 
**The Executive Profile**
We are seeking a respected manufacturing leader with a demonstrated history of transforming operations, developing talent, and delivering measurable business results.
 
 
**The Ideal Candidate Must Have**




+ Proven experience leading large-scale manufacturing organizations.
+ Demonstrated success driving operational and cultural transformation.
+ Experience leading automation, digital manufacturing, or Industry 4.0 initiatives.
+ Strong financial acumen with experience managing capital investments and operating budgets.
+ A track record of improving productivity, quality, throughput, and operational efficiency.
+ Exceptional leadership presence and executive communication skills.
+ The ability to balance strategic vision with executional excellence.
+ Experience building high-performing leadership teams and scalable organizational structures.

**Preferred Leadership Competencies**
**Strategic Leadership**




+ Manufacturing Transformation
+ Business Transformation
+ Enterprise Leadership
+ Strategic Planning
+ Organizational Development

**Operational Excellence**




+ Lean Manufacturing
+ Six Sigma
+ Continuous Improvement
+ Operational Excellence
+ Value Stream Optimization

**Innovation & Growth**




+ Industry 4.0
+ Smart Factory Strategy
+ Digital Manufacturing
+ Manufacturing Innovation
+ Automation Strategy

**Financial & Capital Management**




+ Capital Projects
+ Capacity Planning
+ Facility Expansion
+ Cost Optimization
+ Investment Planning

**Education And Experience Requirements**
Requires a four-year ABET-accredited degree in engineering with significant experience in manufacturing technology; 10+ years of experience in manufacturing operations, including leadership of large-scale initiatives; or any combination of education and experience, which would provide an equivalent background. Advanced degrees and certifications in quality control or advanced manufacturing are preferred.
 
 
**Why BASX?**
BASX continues to invest in advanced manufacturing capabilities, growth initiatives, and operational excellence. This position offers the opportunity to lead meaningful change within an organization committed to innovation, customer success, and long-term growth.
 
 
For leaders who enjoy building organizations, developing talent, optimizing operations, and shaping strategy, this role offers both the challenge and visibility necessary to make a significant impact.
 
 
**Why Redmond, Oregon?**
Located in the heart of Central Oregon, Redmond offers an exceptional quality of life and access to world-class outdoor recreation.
 
 
**Lifestyle Advantages**




+ Hiking, skiing, fishing, mountain biking, golf, and year-round outdoor activities
+ Family-friendly communities and excellent schools
+ One of the fastest-growing regions in the Pacific Northwest
+ No Oregon state sales tax
+ Easy access to Bend, the Cascade Mountains, and major regional airports

**Additional Benefits**




+ Executive-level compensation package
+ Annual incentive opportunity
+ Comprehensive benefits program
+ Relocation assistance available
+ Sponsorship not available

**Build Something That Lasts**
If you are a forward-thinking manufacturing executive who thrives on creating organizational capability, driving transformation, and delivering business results, this is an opportunity to lead at a strategic level while shaping the future of a growing operation.
 
 
**Mental And Physical Functions**
This role requires strategic thinking, technical leadership, and the ability to manage complex initiatives across departments and locations. The Director must be capable of balancing high-level planning with hands-on engagement in manufacturing operations.
 
 

* Communicates effectively in written and spoken form
* Possesses excellent interpersonal and leadership skills
* Demonstrates strong organizational and multitasking abilities
* Works effectively in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment
* Ability to lift up to 50 lbs.
* Sit or stand for up to 95% of work hours
* Regular visits to manufacturing facilities with exposure to seasonal hot and cold temperatures, dust, and chemical fumes

**Work Environment**
The Director, Manufacturing operates in both office and production environments, with frequent interaction across departments and facilities.
 
 

* Work is performed in a combination of office and factory settings
* Exposure to loud noise, dust, temperature fluctuations, and industrial equipment
* Use of personal protective equipment (PPE) is required when on the production floor
* Frequent collaboration with engineering, operations, quality, and executive leadership teams
* This position is designated as a safety-sensitive role and is subject to drug and alcohol testing, including random testing
* Compliance with all company safety and operational policies is mandatory

**Disclaimer**
Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at a time with or without notice. This job description is not an exhaustive list of all functions that the employee may be required to perform, and the employee may be required to perform additional functions. The company reserves the right to revise this job description at any time. The employee must be able to perform the essential functions of the position satisfactorily. If requested, reasonable accommodations may be made to enable employees with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job, absent undue hardship.
 
 
#BASX
 
 
**Benefits And Compensation Summary**
We take care of our people. We offer competitive compensation and robust benefits to all full-time team members, including:
 
 

* Tuition reimbursement
* Paid time-off
* Paid holidays
* Healthcare insurance & Health Savings Accounts
* Profit sharing or Annual Incentive Plan Bonus
* Premium 401(k) plan

identity_held_roles.title: Plant Manager I
identity_held_roles.description:
This position leads all plant operations for a70+ employee, 2 shift, manufacturing site. This leader ensures day-to-day operations are delivered with the aligned objectives of safety-first mindset, customer satisfaction along with growing and developing the leaders within the facility. This position also plays a critical role in developing and executing capital project plans for the facility to enable continuous improvement and growth in market share.

This full-time position reports directly to region General Manager and is located at Liberty Packaging’s manufacturing plant in Houston, Texas

**Duties And Responsibilities**

* Directly lead and supervise a team of direct reports to deliver major site functions across manufacturing, shipping, maintenance, and scheduling.
* Own end-to-end performance for the facility to meet KPIs in the areas of Safety, Quality, Cost, and Delivery. Establish, measure, and monitor performance across facility and root cause performance issues. Develop and deploy plans to drive improvements in manufacturing processes to ensure superior product quality, reduced cycle times, lead times, and minimize overall manufacturing costs.
* Provide day-to-day leadership for manufacturing team decision-making in the areas of production, labor, material costs, design, and production scheduling.
* In partnership with Continuous Improvement function, guide leaders and front-line staff through the identification and deployment of continuous improvement initiatives with an impact on key performance indicators.
* Ensure the right talent and capabilities are in place to meet strategic objectives; accountable for establishing goals, managing performance, and developing teams to ensure short- and long-range objectives are achieved
* Establish a two-way communication & engagement culture to ensure all plant employees are clear on plant performance and connection to business performance, including KPIs.
* Lead key change initiatives across the plant in partnership with regional and functional support systems (e.g., continuous improvement, engineering, human resources, sales, etc.)
* Lead the successful identification, business case design, and execution of capital projects in partnership with functional teams and executive leadership. Ensure multi-year capital plans support market growth and customer delivery
* Ensure employee relations stay connected with open and continuous dialogue
* Develop and grow community engagement presence by representing plant locally in key activities and through execution of frequent employee and community engagement activities
* Own direct P&L responsibility for plant site
* Provide leadership by connecting and being visible to all three shifts daily
* Other duties, as assigned

**Required Education, Experience And Skills**

* Bachelors’ degree and 7+ years manufacturing experience OR 10+ years manufacturing industry experience in lieu of education
* 5+ years people leadership experience
* Experience analyzing downtime, production, and financial variance trends, and identifying actions to deliver expected performance
* Previous experience developing and managing a budget, forecasting, and monitoring results
* Experience with identifying and executing capital projects to drive improvement against KPIs
* Demonstrated experience with organizational effectiveness, operations management, and a proven track record of achieving results
* Experience developing and presenting information to multiple levels of the organization from front-line to executive leadership
* Superior time management, attention to detail, verbal and written communication skills, decision-making, and organization skills
* Excellent computer skills required, including Microsoft Word and Excel skills.
* Demonstrated entrepreneurial spirit

**Preferred Education, Experience And Skills**

* Previous experience with Amtech / CTI or Kiwi
* Previous experience with ERP systems
* Previous experience in corrugated or paper manufacturing
* Lean and / or Continuous Improvement certifications
* Bilingual English / Spanish

**Compensation & Benefits**

The starting base salary range for this position is $110,078 - $137,598 per year plus eligibility in annual bonus program. The compensation posted is the anticipated pay for the position at the time of the posting. We may pay above or below posted amount based on several factors, including, but not limited to education and/or certifications, skills, experience, or work location. Some positions may qualify for additional compensation in the form of bonuses or deferred compensation options.

At LDI, we are pleased to provide employees with a comprehensive benefits package including health/dental/vision insurance options; paid time off; 10 paid holidays; 401(k) plus company matching and annual discretionary profit sharing; flexible spending and health savings account options; life and disability insurance; tuition assistance; wellness and mental health resources, and financial advising services. Eligibility in benefit programs is based on hours worked per week.

**Physical Requirements**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

* Regular sitting, standing, and walking throughout the day to accomplish tasks
* Manual and finger dexterity used regularly with some repetitive finger motions
* Ability to work in front of a computer screen for long periods of time
* Specific vision abilities include close and distance vision; able to identify colors, small letters, and numbers; hand/eye coordination, depth perception and able to adjust focus
* Hearing and speaking
* Other conditions may include frequent reaching, stretching, pushing, pulling, pinching, grasping, and gripping.

**About Our Company**

Comprised of multiple companies with headquarters in New Hope, Minnesota, Liberty Diversified International (LDI) is a privately held company employing more than 1,900 individuals across our manufacturing facilities, production facilities and core business operations in Minnesota, Iowa, Nebraska, Illinois, Mississippi, Texas, Arizona, Virginia, California, and Mexico. With deep roots in the corrugated box manufacturing industry, we operate in the core markets of paper, packaging, workplace products, corrugated plastics and building products.

Since 1918, our values – Caring, Innovation, Trust and Excellence – have guided our day-to-day activities. We believe that when our employees are aligned with these values, we create superior service and solutions for our customers. The LDI family of companies includes Liberty Packaging, Liberty Paper, Liberty Plastics (Custom Solutions and Quarrix Building Products) and Safco.

Liberty Diversified International is an equal opportunity employer and makes all employment decisions without regard to race, color, sex, religion, age, creed, sexual orientation, national origin, marital status, disability, or any other protected class.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Description**
**Description & Requirements**
**About AESC US LLC**
AESC is a global leader in the development and manufacturing of high-performance batteries for zero-emission electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Founded in Japan in 2007 and headquartered in Yokohama, AESC has been building manufacturing capabilities around the world in the U.S., U.K., Europe, Japan and China to serve key markets and leading customers locally for over 14 years. Today, AESC has become the partner of choice for the world's leading OEMs and energy storage providers in North America, Europe, and Asia. Its advanced technology powers over one million electric vehicles and provides more than 15GWh of installed capacity for battery energy systems in over 60 countries.
 
 
AESC is expanding its footprint in the United States, and the Blythewood Repack Operation supports the broader South Carolina production network. AESC is committed to our local communities where it is making its investments, creating jobs, and supporting local charities.
 
 
**About The Role**
The Senior Operations Manager provides comprehensive leadership of manufacturing operations, driving safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective production. This role is responsible for integrating production execution with workforce planning, material flow, equipment availability, quality performance, and operational readiness.
 
 
The successful candidate must possess a broad understanding of plant operations and demonstrate the ability to lead across functions rather than operate solely as a production manager.
 
 
****What You Will Do****

* Direct daily manufacturing operations across assigned shifts and production areas.
* Establish and execute production plans that align labor, equipment, materials, and customer delivery requirements.
* Manage operational KPIs including throughput, OEE, labor productivity, downtime, scrap, cost, and on-time delivery.
* Collaborate with Maintenance and Engineering to ensure equipment availability, preventive maintenance execution, and effective downtime response.
* Partner with Quality to manage manufacturing defects, process compliance, containment, and corrective actions.
* Coordinate with Supply Chain and Logistics to maintain effective material flow, inventory accuracy, and production readiness.
* Lead production supervisors and team leaders, establishing clear expectations for attendance, timekeeping, staffing, overtime controls, and employee performance.
* Manage operating expenses, labor utilization, and production resource requirements.
* Promote a disciplined safety culture with EHS and enforce manufacturing operating standards.
* Support commissioning, production ramp-up, process stabilization, and future plant expansion.
* Develop staffing, succession, and workforce capability plans.
* Complete other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**
****What You Need****

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline, or equivalent substantial manufacturing leadership experience.
* At least 10 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including five years in plant operations leadership.
* Demonstrated accountability for manufacturing performance, staffing, safety, cost, and cross-functional execution.
* Experience with ERP/MES systems, Lean manufacturing, and operational performance management.

****What is "Nice to Have"?****

* Automotive OEM or Tier 1 experience.
* Battery manufacturing experience.
* High-volume automated manufacturing experience.
* Plant launch or greenfield ramp-up experience.

****Travel Requirements****
20% International Travel
 
 
****What We Offer****
Welcome to AESC, where you'll have the opportunity to tackle the world's most fascinating challenges alongside exceptionally talented individuals who are driven to make a difference. We strive to ensure that our employees are well taken care of, enabling them to focus on their work and contribute to our collective mission.
 
 
**We Offer**

* Comprehensive compensation packages including a competitive salary and a rewarding bonus program.
* An inclusive and diverse work environment that fosters and encourages professional and personal development.
* Highly automated, clean, safe, and temperature-controlled production environment.
* Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance.
* HSA and Flexible Spending Accounts.
* 401K with company match.
* Life Insurance (Company paid and additional voluntary life available).
* Paid Vacation and 14 Paid Holidays.
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage (Company Paid).
* Tuition reimbursement.

****Equal Employment Opportunity****
At AESC, we are committed to providing Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) to all individuals. We participate in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. Join us in our passion to design, manufacture, and sell high-performance products, contributing to a sustainable and zero-carbon emission future.
 
 
****Physical Requirements****
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable otherwise qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.
 
 

* Ability to stand, walk, and work on a concrete production floor for extended periods of time.
* Ability to read, write, speak, hear; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach and lift with hands and arms frequently throughout the day.
* Ability to wear all required PPE when working on the production floor.
* Required to occasionally lift, push, pull and/or move up to 10 pounds, and occasionally required to lift, push, pull and/or move up to 35 pounds.

****Work Environment****
The work environment is primarily a semi-automated/automated plant with a concrete floor and is characterized as climate controlled, moderate noise, and forklift traffic. The individual must be able to perform all essential functions as appropriate on the plant floor, in meetings, and with employees, management, customers and suppliers.
 
 
Candidate must perform the essential duties and responsibilities with or without reasonable accommodation efficiently and accurately, and without causing significant safety threat to self or others. The statements made herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this job classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive and inclusive list of all responsibilities, duties, and/or skills required of personnel so classified.
 
 
Hiring is contingent upon successful completion of a drug screen and background check, and verification of the candidate's eligibility to work in the United States. AESC US LLC is a drug-free workplace.

identity_held_roles.title: Sr. Manager, Optimus Operations
identity_held_roles.description:
**What To Expect**
The Senior Manager, Optimus Operations sets the vision and strategic path for Production, Maintenance, and Engineering within a major shop at Tesla’s new Optimus Factory in Austin, Texas. Openings span operations leadership across multiple shops—including Plastics, Machining, Actuators, and Assembly. Each role leads their shop teams and cross-functional partners to achieve Safety, People, Quality, Production/Delivery, and Cost KPI targets.
 
 
This role is responsible for production and resource planning; coaching, mentoring, and developing leaders; launching new Optimus manufacturing processes and programs successfully; and daily tactical planning and execution to achieve the build plan and meet safety, quality, rate, and cost targets. The person in this role must guide the team through complex issues, distill large volumes of data to solve problems, and drive day-over-day continuous improvement in a high-volume, high-precision factory environment.
 
 
This Senior Manager provides hands-on support, leadership, and direction on all operational, team morale, and equipment-related matters. The person in this role builds teams that work cohesively and perform at the highest level—keeping Tesla’s mission and the goals of the Optimus program in mind—while partnering closely with peer shop leaders and factory leadership across the Austin Optimus Factory.
 
 
**What You'll Do**- Set the vision and strategic path for Production and Maintenance in an assigned Optimus shop and lead the team to Safety, People, Quality, Production, and Cost KPI targets
- Drive tactical planning to hit the production build plan with the highest safety, quality, and yield, including identifying bottlenecks and addressing availability, efficiency, and yield constraints
- Launch new Optimus programs and lead production ramps and product/process design changes through resource planning, program management, and partnership with NPI, Manufacturing Engineering, Design Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain
- Guide the team through root cause analysis, first-principles thinking, and data-driven problem solving while maintaining standardized work and quality/safety compliance
- Coach, mentor, and develop Production, Maintenance, and Engineering leaders, instill process standardization and training, and drive continuous improvement
- Lead the maintenance organization on equipment availability, preventive and predictive maintenance, spare parts strategy, and uptime improvements for shop-critical assets
- Build a high-performing team with clear goals and feedback, improve morale with HR, and collaborate with peer shop Senior Managers to share best practices
**What You'll Bring**- Degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, Chemical, Electrical, Materials, or Industrial Engineering preferred, or equivalent experience
- 7–10 years of leadership and manufacturing experience, preferably in automotive, robotics, plastics, precision machining, electromechanical assembly/actuators, general assembly, or another highly technical manufacturing environment
- Analytical, detail-oriented, self-driven critical thinker who communicates proactively and works well in a fast-paced, multicultural factory environment
- Experience with process-improvement methodologies, DOE/statistical methods, lean and world-class manufacturing practices, and standing up or ramping new factories, shops, or production lines
- Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to work under pressure, juggle competing priorities, and meet tight deadlines
- Ability to use structured problem-solving methods such as 8D, fishbone diagrams, and 5-Why analysis to resolve production problems
- High-level leadership and decision-making skills with a strong sense of urgency in a greenfield/new-factory ramp, plus proficiency in MS Office, Visio, CAD, SPC, data-analysis tools, Jira, Tableau/BI dashboards, and project-management tools
**Benefits**
Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:
 
- Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
- Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
- Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
- Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
- Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
- 401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
- Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
- Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
- Employee Assistance Program
- Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
- Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
- Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
- Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
- Tesla Babies program
- Commuter benefits
- Employee discounts and perks program
- Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)
, Tesla

identity_held_roles.description:
**Company And Opportunity Overview**

WNA’s vision is to be a leading entrepreneurial player in terms of market share, agility, and game-changing solutions. WNA is a solution provider, creating value along the supply chain of our customers, from online purchase to their customers.

WNA is headquartered in the Charlotte Metro Area, North Carolina. With around 500 employees and ~$200M of sales, WNA focuses on the retail and distribution market segments with marquee customers such as Walmart, Amazon, and the majority of large grocers and retailers.

In addition to being the largest manufacturer of shopping carts in North America, WNA has three additional main product segments as well as a Service business, providing turnkey solutions for customer guidance (Access Systems), Shelving & Fixtures, and Material Handling products.

Access Solutions provides sophisticated customer guidance and loss prevention systems for major retailers. With German-engineered products and a strong installed base, this segment focuses on protecting existing market share while expanding into adjacent opportunities in smart retail, autonomous store technology, and digital integration.

Additionally, WNA offers a range of digital solutions integrated into our products, including advanced shopping cart containment systems, smart exit gate technology, and innovations for autonomous and semi-autonomous retail stores. We are continuously expanding and enhancing our digital offerings to meet evolving customer needs and drive industry advancement.
